Hold for 5 seconds to charge (roots gather, your eyes glow green), then explosive growth in a 20-block radius: 54 damage, rooted and Poison X for 10 seconds, and a dense thicket that recedes after a few seconds. 51s cooldown.
Living Wall
Conjure a wall of leaves -- look up for a dome, look down for a bridge. Sneak instead to charge your touch with bone meal for 30 seconds. 6.8s cooldown.
Nature’s Blessing

Toggle: your skin turns to bark and leaves. While standing on grass/moss or within 5 blocks of any plant or leaf, gain Regeneration II and +12 to all ability and melee damage. Enemies within 3 blocks of you are poisoned.
Right-clicking any growable plant bone-meals it twice. Plants within 30 blocks grow roughly 50% faster.
Minor regeneration in lush areas. Standing on or against grass/dirt/moss grants Regeneration, Haste, Resistance and Strength.
Attacks and interactions pass straight through short grass, ferns, tall grass and dead bushes instead of being blocked by them.
Thorn Sentry

H: plant a living turret of cactus and flowering azalea where you look (up to 6 blocks). For 15 seconds it turns to the nearest hostile it can see within 14 blocks and spits thorns at it twice a second -- 5 damage and a short Poison each. It never targets you, your squad or any player. One at a time: a new one replaces the old. 25s cooldown.
Spore Cloud

N: breathe out a 4.5-block cloud of spores just ahead of you for 8 seconds. Every half second, enemies inside are poisoned and blinded while you and your squad-mates inside are healed and given Regeneration. 16s cooldown.
message.projecthero.plant.need_nature: You need to be on natural ground, or holding bone meal or a sapling
projecthero.power.power_23_gravity_manip: Gravity Manipulation
Invert

Flip gravity on the creature you are aiming at (30 blocks): it falls UP into the sky for 1.5 seconds (taking 6 if it hits a ceiling), then gravity slams back doubled -- it crashes down for 10 plus fall damage, and everything within 3 blocks of the impact takes 5. No bosses. 9s cooldown.
Heavy Ground

Crush gravity onto a 7-block circle where you aim (24 blocks) for 8 seconds: no enemy inside can jump, every enemy is slowed and takes 3 damage a second, and anything in the air above it -- flying mobs included, up to 14 blocks up -- is dragged down to the floor. Never affects you or your squad. 17s cooldown.
Decide which way gravity pulls: push, crush and levitate, flip a target so it falls into the sky, pin a whole area to the floor, and tear open a black hole.
Gravitic Distortion Serum
Drink the serum, then activate a Gravity Distortion Rig, an Unstable Gravity Plate or a Pressure Chamber — or survive a fall of 14+ blocks.
Gravity Push
A focused gravity pulse, 50-block range, that throws targets away for 12 damage, 1.7s cooldown. Shift for a grab instead — press again to throw for 10.
Gravity Crush

Hold to crush a target up to 50 blocks away for up to 8 seconds, no knockback — 5 damage a second and Slowness II. 17s cooldown on release. Shift for a separate, smaller Gravity Well 20 blocks out (2.5 damage a second, 6 seconds).
Zero-G
Toggle 85% lighter personal gravity for floating and aerial repositioning (no fall damage while it is on). Shift+toggle also fires Gravity Repulsion, pushing nearby enemies away (8.5s cooldown).
Black Hole

Hold for 5 seconds to charge, then rip open a black hole 5 blocks ahead: pulls every enemy within 30 blocks in, 7 damage a second inside 10 blocks, destroys terrain, lasts 15 seconds. Never affects you or your squad. 102s cooldown.
Gravity Lift

Mark up to 10 targets within 20 blocks with Levitation, capped 10 blocks up, for 20 seconds -- free, no cooldown. Shift to slam every marked target down for 17 damage plus fall damage; only the slam pays the 21s cooldown.
Gravitational Nexus

Toggle a gravitational-pressure stance wrapped in a thin violet field: +12 ability damage, +8 melee damage, Speed II and Resistance I, while every enemy within 3 blocks of you takes Slowness IV and 2.5 damage a second. Drains a 115-point bar (~40 seconds); ends on a 17s cooldown.
80% less fall damage, 50% less knockback taken, unaffected by your own gravity effects
message.projecthero.gravity.nexus_low: Your gravitational reserve is too depleted
projecthero.power.power_24_wind_manipula: Wind Manipulation

An air-bender on a Gust meter instead of long cooldowns: throw crescents of wind that cut through whole crowds, rip the air out of a spot to drag enemies in, ride the wind at your back, raise tornadoes and hurricanes, turn arrows aside, glide like an elytra and ride a tornado of your own.
Atmospheric Pressure Serum
Drink inside an active Pressure Chamber / Industrial Fan Array.
Wind Blade

R: throw a crescent of compressed air up to 30 blocks. It passes through every enemy in its path, cutting each one for 12, and breaks up on the first wall. 8 Gust. Shift+R: Blade Flurry — hold to throw 4 smaller blades a second from both hands, 6 each. 12 Gust a second. Hold R: Cyclone Blade.
Cyclone Blade
Hold R: hurl one huge spinning blade of air, 3 blocks across, 40 blocks along your aim: 22 to everything it passes through. 25 Gust, 5s cooldown.
Vacuum

G: rip the air out of the spot you aim at (up to 18 blocks). A vortex opens there and drags every enemy within 10 blocks into its eye, then holds them there, helpless, for 1 second. No bosses. 20 Gust. Shift+G: Wind Push — a 10-block cone of wind: 6 damage and a huge shove to everything in it, plus 8 more if it slams into a wall. Projectiles in the cone are blown away. 15 Gust. Hold G: Suffocate.
Suffocate

Hold G: steal the air round the creature you aim at (up to 20 blocks) for 5s: 3 damage a second, no sprinting or jumping, a collapsing bubble of air round its head. Bosses are only slowed. 30 Gust, 10s cooldown.
Tailwind

X: the wind at your back throws you 14 blocks along your look in a blink, streaking the air behind you. 10 Gust. Shift+X: Updraft — a rising column throws you 12 blocks straight up, and at the top your Glide opens on its own. 15 Gust. While gliding, X is a Gust Boost instead: all your Gust (at least 10) in one blast behind you -- an elytra firework, pushing longer the more Gust it spends (up to 2s). Hold X: Sky Step.
Sky Step
Hold X: walk on air for 10s -- press Jump in mid-air for up to 5 extra jumps, each leaving a little ring of air under your feet. 20 Gust, 12s cooldown.
Tornado

Z: a tornado touches down in front of you and travels where you aimed for 8 seconds. It drags in every enemy within 7 blocks, whirls each one round its funnel for 6 seconds at 4 damage a second, then flings it out high and far. 35 Gust. Shift+Z: Hurricane — a wall of wind rises round you for 5 seconds: projectiles are flung away and mobs are pushed out past it. 30 Gust. Hold Z: Twin Tornadoes.
Twin Tornadoes
Hold Z: two tornadoes orbit you for 8s, shredding every mob they touch for 4 a second and flinging it away (bosses are not flung). 45 Gust, 14s cooldown.
Wind Barrier

V (toggle): a spinning swirl of air in front of you blows every arrow, fireball and other projectile coming at you back where it came from. Tap V again to drop it; it also drops when your Gust runs out. 6 Gust a second. Shift+V: Glide (toggle) — ride the wind like an elytra: steer with your look, dive for speed, pull up to climb (on the ground you hop up first). Lands on its own, or Shift+V again to stop. Free. Hold V: Eye of the Storm.
Eye of the Storm
Hold V: a calm bubble of air 5 blocks round you for 8s: every projectile that comes in stops dead and drops, and mobs are pushed out of it. 35 Gust, 16s cooldown.
Rideable Tornado

C (toggle): a tornado rises under your feet and carries you where you look, bowling through every mob it meets for 6 and throwing it aside. Press C again, or Sneak, to step off — no fall damage. 8 Gust a second. Shift+C: Air Bubble — 20 seconds in a bubble of clean air: you breathe underwater, fire on you goes out, and harmful effects and gas clouds round you (yours and your squad's) are blown away. 20 Gust. Hold C: Downburst.
Downburst

Hold C: slam a column of air down on the spot you aim at (up to 24 blocks): 18 to everything within 6 blocks across, knocked flat and slowed for a moment (bosses only take the damage). 30 Gust, 8s cooldown.

Gust (0–100): every move spends some — Wind Blade 8, Blade Flurry 12 a second, Vacuum 20, Wind Push 15, Tailwind 10, Updraft 15, Tornado 35, Hurricane 30, Wind Barrier 6 a second, Rideable Tornado 8 a second, Air Bubble 20; the hold moves Cyclone Blade 25, Suffocate 30, Sky Step 20, Twin Tornadoes 45, Eye of the Storm 35, Downburst 30 — and it refills 15 a second (25 above y 100) while you are not holding a move.
No fall damage
Projectiles aimed at you veer off 30% of the time
Cobwebs do not slow you down
projecthero.power.power_25_water_manipul: Water Manipulation

A water bender on a Water meter (0–100) instead of long cooldowns, so you can chain move after move. It refills 10 a second, 25 in rain and 40 standing in water. Every move is real moving water — a pressurised bolt, a cutting jet, a whip, a prison sphere, a rolling tidal wall, a geyser, an orbiting shield, a surf wave and a healing swirl — and none of it leaves water blocks behind.
Hydrokinetic Serum
Drink the serum and stay fully underwater for 15 seconds (the serum keeps you breathing), or use a Hydrostatic Test Tank.
Water Shot

R: fire a pressurised bolt of water — 12 damage and a knockback, and it puts out fire on whatever it hits. 8 Water. Shift+R: Hydro Jet — hold to pour a cutting beam of water up to 16 blocks: it cuts through every mob in line for 8 damage a second and pushes them back. 12 Water a second. Hold R: Water Dragon.
Water Dragon
A dragon of water rises from your hands and rams the target you aim at (30 blocks) — 20 damage and a big knockback, and everything near the impact takes 10. 25 Water, 8s cooldown.
Water Whip

G: a whip of water lashes out up to 14 blocks — 12 damage, and it hauls the target in to you. 10 Water. Shift+G: Water Prison — trap the target you aim at (16 blocks) in a sphere of water for 4s: it can't move or breathe and takes 4 drowning damage a second. No bosses. 35 Water, 12s cooldown. Hold G: Whirlpool.
Whirlpool
An 8-block whirlpool opens where you aim (24 blocks) for 6s: it drags mobs to its centre (not bosses) and drowns them for 3 damage a second. 35 Water, 15s cooldown.
Riptide

X: launch yourself like a Riptide trident, spinning through anything in the way — anywhere, wet or dry — with no fall damage from the landing. 15 Water. Shift+X: Wave Ride — surf a wave across land or water, fast, riding up steps and over the top of water and knocking mobs aside — no time limit: 25 Water to start and 1 a second while you ride (no refill till you step off). Shift+X again steps off. Hold X: Hydro Jets.
Hydro Jets
Jets of water from your hands and feet let you fly for 10s, steered like every other flight; landing or holding X again ends it. 30 Water, 18s cooldown.
Tidal Wave

Z: a 7-wide wall of water rears up and rolls 16 blocks forward — 14 damage to everything it reaches, sweeping them along with it, and it puts out fire. 40 Water. Shift+Z: Geyser — a column of water erupts under the target you aim at (24 blocks) and launches it 10 blocks into the air. 20 Water. Hold Z: Tsunami.
Tsunami
A giant wave, 12 wide and 6 tall, rolls 30 blocks — 22 damage, sweeping mobs along with it (not bosses) and putting out fire. No water is left behind. 60 Water, 20s cooldown.
Water Shield

V (toggle): a sphere of water orbits you, swallowing every projectile before it reaches you and putting out any fire around you — tap again to drop it (it also drops when your Water runs out). 6 Water a second. Shift+V: Healing Water — you and every squadmate within 6 blocks heal 8 hearts over 4s and have every harmful effect washed off. 40 Water, 20s cooldown. Hold V: Water Clone.
Water Clone
A clone of you made of water fights for 15s at half your melee damage, and mobs hunting you go for it instead. It bursts into a splash when it ends or is killed (20 health). 40 Water, 25s cooldown.
Aquatic Form

C (toggle): Dolphin's Grace, night vision underwater, and +6 melee damage while you are in water. Free. Shift+C: Draw Water — aim at a water source (12 blocks) to pull it out of the world into your meter (+30 Water), or aim anywhere else to place a source of water there (5 Water). Hold C: Rain Call.
Rain Call
Rain falls in a 16-block circle round you for 60s (only there — the weather stays the same). Standing in it, your Water refills twice as fast and you heal 1 heart every 5s. 30 Water, 90s cooldown.

Water (0–100): every move spends some, and it refills 10 a second — 25 in rain, 40 standing in water — except while you pour the Hydro Jet or keep the Water Shield up — and twice as fast under your own Rain Call.
Water Breathing, always
At home in water: fast swimming, clear sight far into the water (no murky fog) and you mine underwater as fast as on dry ground
30% less damage from fire and lava, and fire on you goes out at once
projecthero.power.power_26_magnetic_mani: Magnetic Manipulation
Magneto Hover

Toggle: push off the metal around you and levitate -- fly freely while there is magnetic metal within a few blocks below or around you, or while you hold an iron item. Leave the metal behind and you drift down gently until you find more. Drains its own 115-point bar (~15 seconds), which refills when you land; field lines crackle over your body while it lifts you.
Disarm

Rip the iron or netherite weapon out of a creature's hand -- or, failing that, a piece of its armour -- and send it clattering to the ground toward you as a real item (4 damage as iron tears loose). Works on players only when PvP ability damage is allowed. Never touches Mjolnir, copper or gold; no metal means no cooldown. 10s cooldown.

Manipulate magnetically reactive metal for combat and movement. Your abilities require actual magnetic material in the environment or on your enemies -- ride it, rip it off them, or hurl it. Copper and gold are not magnetically reactive; netherite can be manipulated but strongly resists magnetic force.
Magnetoreactive Serum
Drink the serum and stand among 16+ iron or copper blocks, bars or anvils for a few seconds — or activate an Electromagnetic Coil.
Ferrous Shot

Launch a nearby magnetic object — a block you look at, a dropped metal item within 30 blocks, a nearby metal block, or (failing all else) a magnetic item from your own inventory — toward your crosshair. Heavier objects fly slower but hit far harder (iron nugget ~7, iron block ~22, anvil/netherite block ~34). 2.5s cooldown; fails with no cooldown if there is no magnetic metal anywhere in reach.
Magnetic Grip

Grab a magnetic block, dropped item, minecart or iron golem and float it on your aim. Heavier objects follow more sluggishly; netherite resists. Activate again to hurl it forward (1.25s between grips).
Polarity Leap

Pull yourself rapidly toward a magnetic object you are looking at, up to 24 blocks. Preserves momentum and cushions the landing briefly — chain leaps between metal to travel. 1.7s cooldown; fails with no cooldown if nothing magnetic is targeted.
Metal Storm

Gather up to 8 nearby magnetic objects into a violent orbit, then launch them at whatever you aim toward. Each object's damage scales with its mass (+20%); damage to any one target is capped at 36 so it can't instantly delete an enemy. Needs at least 2 magnetic objects nearby. 15s cooldown.
Magnetic Crush

Use the magnetic metal an enemy wears or holds against them — crushing damage that scales with how much they carry (one item ~8, full iron armour ~23), plus Slowness and Weakness, and a hard immobilise at 3+ pieces. Netherite takes less damage but is still locked down. No metal on the target means no effect and no cooldown. 7.6s cooldown.
Magnetic Sense

Toggle: highlight nearby magnetically reactive objects — iron blocks and ore, iron bars, chains, anvils, rails, lanterns, minecarts, lodestone, netherite, dropped iron, and metal-equipped enemies. Copper and gold are never highlighted.
Dropped magnetic items within 30 blocks drift toward you, hopping over ledges; controlled objects can't hurt you
Objects you are currently controlling never damage their owner
projecthero.power.power_27_size_manipula: Size Manipulation

Change body scale -- every change eases over a second -- for stealth, mobility or giant strength: shrink foes with a punch, ride mobs when tiny, and pick them up when huge. Neither form is universally superior.
Mass Compression Serum
Drink the serum, then activate a Mass Compression Chamber (found at Government Experiment Sites, or craft one).
Giant Punch
Enlarge the striking arm for a wide sweeping hit: 12 damage (+6 in Large, +18 in Giant, a third in Tiny) -- its reach scales with how big you are (roughly 4x in Giant form). 2.55s cooldown.
Stomp
Stomp for a ground shockwave: 9.6 damage (+6 Large, +18 Giant) and a slow, with a radius that scales with your size (much wider as a giant). 6.8s cooldown.
Tiny Form
Toggle (X): shrink to about half a block tall over one second, in a puff of particles. Press again to ease back to normal size.
Giant Form

Toggle (Z): grow to ~15 blocks tall over one second, in a burst of particles -- ~16-block reach, +18 damage on every move, 3-block leaps, and creatures you walk over are trampled. Drains the Size Strain bar (575, ~26s); once you shrink back it slowly recharges on its own.
Tiny Dash
Rapidly dash forward with a burst of speed and brief damage resistance -- duck under attacks or slip through a gap. 4.25s cooldown.
Large Form
Toggle (C): grow to about 6 blocks tall over one second, in a burst of particles -- ~7-block reach, +6 damage, a wide pickup radius, and 3-block leaps. Press again for normal size.
Form-dependent reach, speed, step height and hitbox changes
Every form takes 65% less fall damage
Shrink Punch

H: a punch that shrinks its target to half size for 8 seconds -- a smaller hitbox, shorter reach and 40% weaker hits -- plus 8 damage. Bosses take the hit but keep their size. A miss costs nothing. 10s cooldown.
Mount

N: in Tiny form, climb onto the mob you are looking at and ride it (up to 60 seconds). In Large or Giant form, pick up the mob you are looking at (anything under 60% of your height) and carry it in your hand for up to 20 seconds. Press N again to hop off or throw it. It is always let go safely if you change form, die or lose the power. 2s cooldown after.
projecthero.guide.iron_man.era1.body: The first five suits are clunky but hit hard: Mk I Cave-Forged, Mk II Golden Avenger, Mk III Classic, Mk IV Hydro and Mk V Stealth. They only go on and come off in a Stark Gantry (stand on its floor and press H -- the arms build the suit onto you), and they are only repaired there (racked on a Suit Platform within 20 blocks of a complete Gantry, or worn on the floor). Every key R, G, X, Z, V and C has a tap move and a Shift move (Shift+C is the emergency eject); hold Left Alt for the list, or see the suit pages below. The Mk III, Mk IV and Mk V fly (double-tap Space); the Mk I rocket-jumps and the Mk II hovers on its boot jets. The later suits (Mk VI Suitcase to Hulkbuster I) are Era II: built from the Era II tab of the Stark Workbench, each with its own portable form.
projecthero.guide.iron_man.era1_energy.b: Era I suits run on their Arc Reactor. Every move costs energy when it goes off; held and toggled moves (the flamethrower, the hover, the tractor beam, the camo...) drain it every second they run, and so does flight (Mk III, Mk IV and Mk V: 2 a second, 4 sprinting). It recharges slowly by itself and fast (+50 a second) in the Gantry. Not enough for a move shows LOW POWER. At 0 the suit BROWNS OUT: no moves, no flight or hover -- the armour still protects you -- until the reactor is back to 10%. The HUD shows INTEGRITY and REACTOR bars above the keys.
projecthero.guide.iron_man.era1_eject.bo: Stuck in an Era I suit far from a Gantry? Hold Shift+C for 3 seconds: you are shot out of the back of the suit, and the empty armour stands there for a moment, then folds itself into a Suit Crate (it keeps the pieces' integrity and energy). Right-click the crate to read the suit's state; right-click it with iron ingots to patch it up (4% of its integrity each); Shift+right-click it to put the suit back on by hand, anywhere -- 30 seconds of fitting and hammering. Break the crate to carry it (heavy -- Slowness while you carry it) and place it again wherever you like. Used on a Stark Gantry floor the arms put the suit on, and on a Suit Platform in a Gantry's range it racks the suit.
projecthero.guide.iron_man.era1_eject.li: hold 3 s: emergency eject into a Suit Crate
projecthero.guide.iron_man.workbench.bod: The Stark Fabricator is now the Stark Workbench: a two-block desk (it takes the block to your right). Up close it projects a turning hologram of the suit you are building -- built pieces bright, the rest a wireframe -- with a ring and two floating screens. Its screen has era tabs (Era I now, the rest coming), the suit list, a hologram preview you can drag to spin, the suit's stats, the selected piece's recipe (missing parts in red) and a Build button that loads the blueprint and the parts for you. Old one-block Fabricators keep working and grow into the full desk once the block to their right is free.

projecthero.combo.strength_flight: Super Strength + Flight: Ground Slam / Dive Bomb scale with fall speed, and Sneak+N fires METEOR SLAM — rocket skyward and come down in a 26-damage crater (40 s).
projecthero.combo.speed_electrokinesis: Super Speed + Electrokinesis: sprinting builds charge for your next electrical ability, and Sneak+N fires THUNDER SPRINT — a 14-block lightning dash that shocks (18) and slows everything in the path (30 s).
projecthero.combo.water_electrokinesis: Water + Electrokinesis: wet targets take extra electrical damage, and Sneak+N fires STORM SURGE — an electrified tidal ring, 22 damage and a heavy slow around you (35 s).
projecthero.combo.geokinesis_strength: Geokinesis + Super Strength: stronger earth attacks, and Sneak+N fires BOULDER BARRAGE — rip up three boulders and hurl them (30 s).
projecthero.combo.cryokinesis_water: Cryokinesis + Water: Sneak+N fires GLACIER FLOOD — a freezing flood that deals 16, freezes and roots everything within 8 blocks (35 s).
projecthero.combo.pyrokinesis_flight: Pyrokinesis + Flight: a fiery trail at high speed, and Sneak+N fires COMET DASH — burn 16 blocks forward, 16 damage and ignition to everything you pass (30 s).
projecthero.combo.energy_absorption_lase: Energy Absorption + Laser Vision: stored energy tops up your heat, and Sneak+N fires SOLAR LANCE — a 40-block, 30-damage beam (40 s).
projecthero.combo.wind_fire: Wind + Pyrokinesis: Sneak+N fires FIRE TORNADO — a burning vortex where you aim that drags enemies in for 6 seconds (45 s).
projecthero.combo.shadow_teleportation: Shadow + Teleportation: Sneak+N fires UMBRAL LEAP — vanish and reappear up to 28 blocks away, blinding and hitting everyone near the landing (25 s).
projecthero.combo.speedster_set: Speedster build: Super Speed + Super Regeneration + Electrokinesis.
projecthero.combo.crystal_hero_set: Crystal Hero build: Crystalkinesis + Sonic Scream + Shockwave Manipulation.
projecthero.combo.psychic_set: Psychic build: Telekinesis + Teleportation + Invisibility / Light Manipulation.

projecthero.guide.overview.body: Project Hero turns Minecraft into a superhero sandbox. Alongside iconic heroes like Thor, Iron Man, Spider-Man, Max Steel, the Punisher, Green Lantern, Wolverine, the Titan Shifter, One For All, Moon Knight, the Hulk, the Super Soldier, the Kryptonian and the speedster (Super Speed, awakened by the Speed Force), you can undergo experimental mutations to permanently gain minor powers. The mutations are being remade one by one: Super Strength, Laser Vision and Super Regeneration are available now, the rest return as they are rebuilt.
projecthero.guide.powerclass.body: Every power is either Primary or Secondary. Primary powers are who you are: Thor, Iron Man, Spider-Man, Max Steel, the Punisher, Green Lantern, Wolverine, the Titan Shifter, One For All, the Hulk, Moon Knight, the Super Soldier, the Kryptonian and the 27 mutations (Super Speed is a mutation again since v0.14.21). You hold ONE Primary power at a time (v0.14.4). The mutations count as one group that shares that single slot (up to 3 of them stack, as before). Gaining any hero power -- however you get it, lifting Mjolnir included -- replaces the hero power or mutations you had: become Spider-Man, then lift Mjolnir, and you are Thor and nothing else. Gaining a mutation replaces your hero power. Secondary powers ride on top of a Primary one. The Symbiote is the only Secondary power for now. It shares a host only with Spider-Man (Black Suit) or the Punisher (Agent Venom), so gaining any other Primary power also removes the Symbiote. Worlds saved under the old two-power rule keep only their newest hero power the next time you join.
projecthero.guide.unique_powers.body: Server owners can make every hero power one-of-a-kind with /gamerule projectheroUniquePowers true. While it is on, only one player at a time can hold each hero power (the Symbiote too; mutations are not limited). Trying to gain a taken power fails and tells you who holds it, and your serum or item is kept. A power frees up when its holder loses it or swaps it for another. Operators: /projecthero uniquepowers list shows who holds what, and /projecthero uniquepowers release <power> frees one.
projecthero.guide.controls.title: Controls
projecthero.guide.controls.body: Every power uses the same six ability keys, named Ability 1 to Ability 6 in Options > Controls (R, G, Z, X, C, V by default: Ability 1 = R, Ability 2 = G, Ability 3 = Z, Ability 4 = X, Ability 5 = C, Ability 6 = V). What each key does depends on your active power (or on Thor, when you hold Mjolnir). Two utility keys sit beside them: Utility 1 (H) and Utility 2 (N).
projecthero.guide.controls.select: H   Utility 1 - with a mutation selected, H is its Utility 1 ability and Shift+H opens the power wheel (switch which mutation occupies the keys). The power wheel is only for mutations: Hero-Tier powers have none. Hero powers use H first: Iron Man's faceplate, Max Steel's helmet, the Symbiote suit, the Hulk, Moon Knight's suit, Wolverine's claws, Thor's armour. Alt+H always fires your mutation's Utility 1.
projecthero.guide.controls.info: I   Your Power - open a quick reference for your active power and all of its abilities.
projecthero.guide.controls.squad: P   Squad - team roster: teammate health, powers, position and distance. See the Squads chapter.
projecthero.guide.controls.flight_mode: ,   Flight Mode - Regular or Physics flight for every hero flight. See Flying below.
projecthero.guide.flight.body: Every hero flight steers the same way (v0.14.16). Take off with your power's usual gesture (usually a double-tap of Jump). W flies toward where you are looking and S flies backward, away from it -- look up to climb, down to dive. A and D slide sideways, Space rises and Sneak sinks straight down. Let go of everything and you ease into a steady hover: no falling, no drift. Sprint flies faster, and some powers add their own boost (Green Lantern: Sneak+Sprint; Kryptonian: X in the air; the Flight mutation: hold C for Afterburner, which sprint-flying and its Lift meter pay for). Your flight's energy or stamina bar still applies. Touch the floor and you stop flying (v0.15.19, every hero flight: Iron Man and the Repulsor Boots, Nova, Kryptonian, Thor, Green Lantern, Max Steel's Turbo Flight and the rest) -- exactly as if you had switched it off yourself. Not in the first half-second after you take off, and not while you are still climbing, so taking off from the ground always works.
projecthero.guide.flight.physics: Physics Flight (v0.16.2): press , (comma) to open the Flight Mode menu and pick Regular or Physics Flight -- the choice is saved on your computer and applies to every hero flight. Physics Flight flies like a jet: W is throttle and builds speed instead of jumping to it, S is an air brake, and your speed carries -- turns swing your path round instead of snapping, diving gains speed and climbing loses some, and with no throttle you glide slowly down to a hover. Mouse up / down pitches the nose and mouse left / right rolls you, so roll and pull back to turn; A and D turn the nose. Your view rolls with you (the HUD stays level), a roll keeps going for a moment after a flick, and with nothing pressed you gently level out, banking into your turn. Loops and full barrel rolls work. Every hero keeps the same top speed, sprint speed and boosts as in Regular. The menu can swap mouse left / right to turning (A / D then roll), set the roll sensitivity, invert the roll, and switch the auto-level or the camera roll off. Other players see you bank and roll.
projecthero.guide.mutation.body: 1. Study a research note to learn a mutation exists. 2. Craft the power’s reagent from obscure materials, then brew it with the listed base potion to make an unstable serum. 3. Drink the serum — you gain a temporary Unstable Mutation. 4. Before it fades, perform the required exposure event (a dangerous accident, or a laboratory device). 5. Survive it and the power is yours forever: UNUSUAL MUTATION DETECTED.
projecthero.guide.mutation.capacity: You may permanently own up to 3 minor mutations (server-configurable). Only one occupies the six ability slots at a time — switch with the power wheel (Shift+H; the wheel is only for mutations, never for Hero-Tier powers; Super Speed stands alone, so it has nothing to switch to). Switching never resets cooldowns or duplicates passives. The mutations share your single Primary slot: a serum adds a mutation to the ones you carry, but replaces any hero power you hold (and removes a bonded Symbiote). In the other direction, gaining any hero power replaces every mutation you carry. A Power Suppressor strips everything — every hero power, every mutation and a bonded Symbiote.
projecthero.guide.mutation.research: Research advances: Research Found → Serum Stabilized → Exposure Survived → Mutation Confirmed. Once confirmed, the full recipe is permanently recorded and reproducible for teammates.
projecthero.guide.mutation.notes: Spare notes (v0.15.11): put four Damaged Research Notes about the same power and a Glass Bottle anywhere in a crafting grid to piece that power’s serum back together -- the same serum the brewing route makes. Four blank notes (no subject, or a power that is switched off) and a bottle make a Mutagenic Serum instead. Notes about different powers never mix.
projecthero.guide.structures.body: Seven rare structures generate above ground across the Overworld. Explore to find them; six hold research notes, thematic ingredients and usually a laboratory device, and the Gamma Lab holds the Gamma Serum.
projecthero.guide.structure.research_fac: Brewing gear, copper/redstone machinery and a light projector. Linked to Flight, Laser Vision, Telekinesis, Wind and Gravity research.
projecthero.guide.structure.meteor_impac: A scorched crater with an unusual central crystal. Linked to Energy Absorption, Flight, Laser Vision and Density.
projecthero.guide.structure.power_statio: Coils, generators, Charged Copper Plates and an Overloaded Redstone Coil. Linked to Electrokinesis, Super Strength and Magnetism -- and the Charged Copper Plates can awaken the Speed Force (Super Speed).
projecthero.guide.structure.geological_s: Lapis, amethyst and resonance equipment. Linked to Geokinesis, Crystalkinesis and Density.
projecthero.guide.structure.government_s: A rare fenced compound with prototype compression machines. Linked to Density, Size and Gravity.
projecthero.guide.structure.hydrostatic_: A small pump station near water with a Hydrostatic Test Tank. Linked to Water Manipulation.
projecthero.guide.devices.body: Craftable, reusable devices that reliably trigger a specific exposure event. Most fire on a redstone pulse; some on right-click. Stand within a few blocks with an active serum.
projecthero.guide.devices.wardrobe.manne: Mannequin: an armour stand shaped like a blank wooden player, so every suit fits it the way it fits you (the Spider-Man suits included). Place it, right-click armour or a held item onto it and right-click to take one off (where you click picks the piece), Shift+right-click to swap your whole suit with its suit, punch it twice to pick it up with everything it wore. Recipe: an armour stand ringed by three white wool, a stick below.
projecthero.guide.devices.wardrobe.wardr: Wardrobe: three blocks wide and two tall, facing you when placed (it needs the room). It keeps ten full suits. The selected one stands on the mannequin in the middle and the brass plate on top shows its number; the next four each way hang on the left and right rails. Right-click the left or right side to move the selection that way. Shift+right-click the middle (whatever you hold) to swap your whole suit with the selected one (wear nothing to put it on, or store yours in an empty slot). A plain right-click on the middle works like an armour stand for the selected suit: hold a piece to hang it, empty-handed to take the piece you click. Break any part and the whole Wardrobe drops, with every suit in it. Recipe: planks round a mannequin, a gold ingot on top and a chest below.
projecthero.guide.combos.body: Owning two complementary powers unlocks synergies (they apply passively where relevant):
projecthero.guide.thor.body: Thor is a Primary power, rarer and stronger than any minor mutation -- Mjolnir does not drop from any mob or chest; you have to find a natural hammer and prove yourself worthy of it.
projecthero.guide.thor.step.find_hammer: Find a hammer -- hold a Lightning Rod and Sneak + right-click a villager; 25 emeralds buys a direction to the nearest free Mjolnir
projecthero.guide.thor.step.worthy: Become a Hero of the Village -- defeat a raid or a Supervillain Raid to earn the effect
projecthero.guide.thor.step.lift: Lift the hammer while Hero of the Village is active -- it binds to you instantly and the effect is used up
projecthero.guide.thor.bind: Binding makes Thor your one Primary power: every other hero power and any mutations you carry are replaced, and a bonded Symbiote is removed. It only ever happens at the moment of lifting -- once Hero of the Village runs out, an unbound hammer will not move for you again until you earn the effect again. Someone else who lifts a hammer already bound to another player may carry it while their own effect lasts, but it never binds to them and the owner is untouched. Once you are Thor you can pick up your own hammer freely, and Sneak + right-click still unbinds and rebinds it.
projecthero.guide.thor.perk.speed: +18% movement speed and some knockback resistance
projecthero.guide.thor.perk.damage_reduc: 80% less damage from every source -- falls and lightning can never hurt you
projecthero.guide.thor.perk.hammer_damag: Mjolnir itself hits for 11 swung, 18 thrown
projecthero.guide.thor.perk.hud: Your ability bar stays on screen the whole time you're bound to a hammer, even when Mjolnir isn't in your hands
projecthero.guide.thor.ability.call_mjol: Calls Mjolnir -- or Stormbreaker, if you have one bound (see Stormbreaker below) -- to your hand from anywhere. A plain right-click throws it instead -- no key needed -- and a thrown hammer flies straight past your squadmates. If it is already somewhere in your inventory, it swaps straight into your main hand and whatever you were holding takes its old slot. A recalled hammer lands in your main hand if it is free, otherwise the next open inventory slot -- never the off hand -- and if your hand and inventory are both full, it goes into your hand anyway and drops what you were holding. Also ends Hammer Volley early.
projecthero.guide.thor.ability.lightning: Mjolnir is thrust to the sky and a 22-damage lightning bolt crashes down on whatever you are aiming at -- with a soft aim assist onto the nearest enemy if your aim is slightly off -- then arcs on to nearby hostile mobs. The bolt goes straight past a squadmate standing in the way.
projecthero.guide.thor.ability.thunder_f: Shift+G: hurl the weapon in your hand (with Mjolnir and Stormbreaker both in hand, the main-hand one) down at the ground you are aiming at, up to 24 blocks away. It slams in and stays there while a bolt hits it and the ground around it is covered in lightning for 4 seconds: a 5-block field that shocks every hostile mob standing in it for 4 damage every half second and slows it. It never touches you, your squad or anyone's pets, sets nothing on fire and breaks no blocks. Then the weapon flies back to your hand (press R to call it back early). 15-second cooldown -- the thin amber bar along the bottom of the G box.
projecthero.guide.thor.ability.lightning: Brace the hammer out in front of you and channel a thick, crackling beam of lightning from its head for 8 damage per tick while held. It passes through your squadmates without touching them.
projecthero.guide.thor.ability.god_of_th: Hold for 5 seconds to charge (a bar shows the buildup): you raise Mjolnir to the sky, lightning gathers on it and, past half charge, bolts reach down into it. On release you bring it down and a barrage of lightning hits the point you are aiming at -- 100 damage and a shockwave rolling out across 7 blocks. Drains 100 Storm Energy. Your squad is never caught in the blast.
projecthero.guide.thor.ability.thundercl: A two-handed overhead slam: a 7-block shockwave races out over the ground, dealing 22 damage and knocking back and slowing every enemy around you. Costs 10 Storm Energy. Squadmates are left completely alone -- no damage, no shove, no slow.
projecthero.guide.thor.ability.hammer_vo: Fling Mjolnir up and away: it autonomously strikes every enemy within 25 blocks in sequence, closest first -- never your squadmates or their pets. If only one is in range, it orbits and re-strikes them every 2 seconds instead; with nothing in range it circles you at a 3-block radius until a target appears. Lasts 12 seconds, or until you call the hammer back early. 32-second cooldown.
projecthero.guide.thor.ability.chain_lig: Thrust the hammer forward and a crackling bolt strikes everyone in a cone in front of you for 18 damage, arcing from target to target. It skips your squadmates and their pets.
projecthero.guide.thor.ability.weapon_se: Opens a small screen with Mjolnir and Stormbreaker, each with an Active / Inactive switch. Only Active weapons answer R: switch one off and R never calls it, even when it is the closer or the only one bound to you -- the other is then called on its own. Switch both off and R calls nothing (it tells you so). Both start Active, and your choice is kept through relogging and death.
projecthero.guide.thor.flight.body: Double-tap Jump while holding Mjolnir (or Stormbreaker) to fly: 18 blocks a second, 36 sprinting. Touch the ground to land.

projecthero.guide.iron_man.mark_9.body: The INFERNO armour, built for the Nether: charcoal plate, bronze trim, heat-sink fins on the back. 3200 integrity, absorbs 55%; 4/9/7/4, toughness 4.5; flies like the Mk VIII Space, 24 (44); +10 melee; repairs 12/s after 10 s out of combat. With all four pieces on, fire and lava do nothing (the pieces float in lava like netherite). Built after the Mk VIII Space, before the Hulkbuster. It packs into the Mk IX Heat Case: with all four loose pieces in your inventory, right-click one. C (or right-clicking the case) sets the case down, its leaves swing open on a glow of heat and the plate climbs on; hold Shift+C to fold it back into your hand. Both work in fire and lava, and if a fold leaves you standing in the heat, the case gives you 10 seconds of Fire Resistance to get clear. With the full suit on you swim through lava fast (look where you want to go, Space up, Shift down) and see far through it. HEAT SINK (0-100, HUD): fills in lava and fire and from your fire moves, vents slowly (fast in water or rain); from 50 the plating is HOT (fire moves +25%); at 100 the fire moves lock until V vents it below 85. R Fire Blast (21 + fire, splash 8) / Shift hold Inferno Stream (a flame cone, 9 every half second). G Magma Fist (26 + fire, big knockback) / Shift Eruption (30 in 5 blocks, enemies thrown up burning). X Afterburner (a dash, 24, fire trail) / Shift Lava Geyser (rocket up on a flame column, 16 below you; no fall damage). Z Magma Bomb (lobbed, 24 in 3.5 blocks + a burning pool for 5 s) / Shift Firestorm (8 incendiary missiles, 16 each). V Heat Dump (needs 20 heat: the whole sink vents as a fire nova, up to 46 in 12 blocks) / Shift Molten Lash (a whip of molten alloy across the front: 22 + fire in a 7-block arc, enemies yanked toward you). C Thermal Siphon (draws heat from fires, lava and burning enemies within 8 blocks, puts the fires out and repairs the suit 15 per source). Reactor (v0.16.7): 1700 energy on top of the heat sink, +2.5/s, the Inferno Stream drains 4/s.

projecthero.guide.iron_man.body: Craft an Arc Reactor and right-click it to become Tony Stark. Tony Stark grants the knowledge to build and operate advanced Iron Man technology — the Stark Workbench, Stark components, and the Iron Man suit progression. Without the Tony Stark power, Stark technology simply does not respond: the Workbench will not open, and Iron Man armour is ejected from unauthorized wearers.
projecthero.guide.iron_man.step.arc_reac: Craft the Arc Reactor Mk1 (Iron, Copper, Redstone Block)
projecthero.guide.iron_man.step.fabricat: Build the Stark Workbench (Iron Blocks, Pistons, Crafting Table, Reactor Core, Diamond)
projecthero.guide.iron_man.step.mark_v: Develop the Mk V Stealth (Stealth Coating)
projecthero.guide.iron_man.step.mark_vii: Develop the Mk VIII Space armour (Thermal Shielding)
projecthero.guide.iron_man.step.mark_8: Develop the Hulkbuster I Bruiser (Hydraulic Frame)
projecthero.guide.iron_man.recipes: Stark components craft at a normal crafting table or in the Stark Workbench (same ingredients either way, and most make 2-4 at a time). Every suit piece after the Mk I is fabricated only, with that mark's blueprint in the slot -- pick the piece and "View more" lists exactly what it needs. Each piece uses the Fabricator's full energy buffer, which refills on its own in 2.5 minutes (a Reactor Core or Arc Reactor in an input slot tops it up faster). The Mk I is built at a normal crafting table from Metal Plating wrapped around the matching iron armour piece: an Iron Helmet for the helmet, an Iron Chestplate for the chestplate, Iron Leggings for the leggings and Iron Boots for the boots.
projecthero.guide.iron_man.controls: Wearing a suit the keys are R / G / X / Z / V (and C on the Era I suits) -- each with a tap move and a Shift move on their own cooldowns (see the suit pages below, or press I for the spec sheet) -- and C. Double-tap jump in the air to fly, as long as you like (the Mk I cannot: it rocket-jumps; the Mk II hovers on its boot jets); touching the ground ends a flight. Speeds: Mk II hover (18 sprinting), Mk III 20 (32), Mk VI Suitcase 18 (28), Hydro 14 (22), Stealth 20 (34), Centurion 22 (38), Space 24 (44), Hulkbuster a 10 b/s hover. Unarmoured, C puts on any armour you are carrying; the Mk VI Suitcase lives in its Briefcase (right-click it). With the Stark Glasses on, Sneak + C opens the Call Armour picker for your Mk IX Inferno and Hulkbuster I (the Hulkbuster drops in from orbit); the Colantotte Bracelets call the Mk VIII Space. Iron Man armour makes you immune to fall damage, and flying hard into the ground slams down for 20 damage.
projecthero.guide.iron_man.mark_1_v2.bod: The Mk I rebuilt in polished gold at the Workbench: the first repulsors and a short boot-jet hover instead of real flight. Integrity 850, absorbs 32%, reactor 800 (1.5 a second). Moves:
projecthero.guide.iron_man.comic.body: The later suits (Mk VI onwards) have no suit energy -- the Era I suits run on their reactor, see above. Every key (R, G, X, Z, V) has a tap move and a Shift move, each on its own cooldown -- nothing else limits them, and flight is unlimited (except the Mk I and Mk II, which jump and hover). Hold Left Alt to list a key strip's moves; the I key shows the full spec sheet.
projecthero.guide.iron_man.comic.integri: Integrity is the suit's resource. While it has any, the suit absorbs its share of every hit (Mk I 20% up to the Hulkbuster 60%) -- that share comes off the integrity instead of you. At 0 integrity the suit is DISABLED: no flight, no abilities, heavy Slowness and a dark visor until a Suit Platform or Stark Gantry repairs it. The Mk VII and Mk VIII also repair themselves after 10 seconds out of combat; the Hulkbuster has its Replacement Pod.
projecthero.guide.iron_man.step.mark_1: Craft the Mk I Cave-Forged at a crafting table (grey iron)
projecthero.guide.iron_man.step.mark_1_v: Upgrade the whole Mk I into the Mk II Golden Avenger (Workbench: each Mk I piece + Gilded Plating)
projecthero.guide.iron_man.step.mark_2: Develop the Mk VI Suitcase (carried in the Briefcase)
projecthero.guide.iron_man.step.mark_4: Develop the Mk IV Hydro (Pressure Hull)
projecthero.guide.iron_man.step.mark_6: Develop the Mk VII Silver Centurion
projecthero.guide.iron_man.screens.body: With the faceplate closed the helmet HUD frames your view: suit name, ENERGY and INTEGRITY with exact values top-left, extra meters only when they matter (air, heat, flight burst, overload, missile reload) and an ability strip above the hotbar with each key, its icon and a cooldown sweep -- hold Left Alt to read the slot names. Call Armour shows every suit as a card with a turning 3D preview, charge, integrity and where it is (arrow keys + Enter work too). The Suit Platform previews the stored suit with full charge / integrity bars; every docked suit charges at its own Arc Reactor rate (the same as worn, never the halved flight rate) and repairs 5 integrity a second, with welding arms rising out of the pad while it works. The picker (Stark Glasses only: the Mk IX Inferno and the Hulkbuster I) also lists armour carried in your pack -- pick it to send those pieces home to your platform; Sneak + C in a suit does nothing on the Mk I to Mk VIII (only the Mk IX and the Hulkbuster open the picker / send themselves home that way). The Stark Fabricator has a tab per suit piece and a checklist of what you have against what the piece needs. A Blank Blueprint opens the Mk I -> Hulkbuster I track: lit marks can be stamped, locked ones say which suit to finish first. The weapon wheel (V on the Mk III, Mk IV and Mk VIII) is open only while you hold V: point at a wedge to read what it does and let go of V to equip it (let go over the centre to keep what you have). Its Homing Missiles option fires four missiles that lock on to whatever is nearest your crosshair (within 30 blocks); Micro-Missiles fly straight where you aim. Every suit's eyes, arc reactor and palm repulsors glow in the dark, and the Mk V Stealth's X blades slide out of its gauntlets.
projecthero.guide.iron_man.suit_up.body: A suit that builds itself onto you (a called suit, the Hulkbuster, a Protocol Phoenix rescue -- a suit you put on from your pack goes on by hand instead, see below) takes 3 seconds per piece, boots first, then legs, chest and helmet: the inner layer closes around you in two halves, then the outer plating fills in one pixel at a time. You strike one of four random suit-up poses that change with the piece being built and react as each one locks home. Nothing can hurt you while a suit is assembling onto you -- piece by piece, from the Suit Platform's arms, flying in when called, out of the Mk VI Suitcase's briefcase or the Mk VIII pod -- until the moment it comes online. The suit only comes online -- abilities and flight unlocked -- once every piece is fully built. Called armour flies in from its platform first; the Mk VIII Space arrives by pod and the Mk VI Suitcase unfolds from its briefcase.
projecthero.guide.iron_man.hand_build.bo: Era I suits (Mk I-V) never do this -- they only go on in a Stark Gantry. For the later suits: press C with a suit in your pack -- no gantry, no call -- and you put it on yourself, by hand. You can't walk, jump, fly or use abilities until it is done, and nothing can hurt you meanwhile. The Mk I takes 30 seconds: you sit down on the floor, pick up each boot and greave, fit it round your legs, hammer it shut with sparks flying and pull the straps tight; then you stand up, pull the chestplate over your head, hammer the rivets and the bracer, lift the helmet on, tap it home and pull the faceplate down. The other suits take 25 seconds and are the workshop version, standing the whole time: step into the boots and clamp them, slap the greaves shut, clamp the chestplate and press the arc reactor home, a few hammer taps, a wrench on the bolts, and the faceplate comes down last. The hammer and wrench are only for show -- you never get them. Carrying only some of the pieces makes it shorter. The Mk VI Suitcase and Mk IX Inferno still deploy from their cases, a Mk VIII Space with the Colantotte Bracelets still wraps on in 4 seconds, the Stark Gantry still fits a suit with its arms and the Hulkbuster still builds itself on. Your view no longer zooms in while you are held still. Log out or change dimension mid-build and the suit finishes going on at once; die and it stops where it is.
projecthero.guide.iron_man.suit_down.bod: Era I suits (Mk I-V) only come off in a Stark Gantry (or by the Shift+C emergency eject). (v0.16.7: C is a kit move on every Era II suit now -- they come off by holding Shift+C, which folds them into their portable form, or with Remove in a Stark Gantry.) Before that, plain C in a Mk VII or VIII took it off by hand: you took it off yourself, held still the whole time (your view no longer zooms in), with every piece going into your main inventory with its charge. The Mk I comes off by hand in about 18 seconds: you push the faceplate up, knock the helmet bolts loose with the hammer (a clank and a spray of sparks at each), wrench the helmet off and toss it aside; knock the bracer and chest rivets loose and haul the chestplate up over your head; hammer the knee bolts, loosen the hip straps and pull the greaves off; then knock the ankle clamps open, step out of the boots and toss them too. Each plate is held for a moment, dropped, and vanishes with a clank as it hits the floor. The other suits (v0.15.19) came off by hand the same way, piece by piece off your body, in about 20 seconds -- with the wrench instead of the hammer: you push the faceplate up, ratchet the bolt at the back of the neck loose and lift the helmet off; pop the gauntlet clamps, ratchet the gauntlet bolt, twist the arc reactor out (the suit powers down) and haul the chestplate up over your head; ratchet the hip bolts, pop the greaves open and pull them off; then ratchet the ankle bolts and step out of the boots. Every plate is held for a moment, dropped beside you and vanishes as it hits the floor, just like the Mk I, and everyone nearby sees it. The pieces still end up in your main inventory. The Mk VI Suitcase still folds into its briefcase and the Hulkbuster still un-builds. Log out or change dimension mid-way and it finishes at once; die and it stops where it is (whatever is still on you drops like any armour).

projecthero.guide.squads.body: A squad is a group of players who cannot hurt each other. Nothing one squadmate does lands on another — not a sword, not an arrow, not a grenade, not a repulsor beam, not a 55-damage Psychic Detonation. That is the whole point: these powers are built to level a hillside, and without a squad you cannot use half of them anywhere near a friend. The one exception is a Hulk on a rampage: he stops being anyone's squad-mate until it ends, so he can hurt his squad and they can hurt him back (PvP permitting). The leader can also switch FRIENDLY FIRE on (/squad friendlyfire on, or the button on the squad screen): then squadmates' hits land on each other like anyone else's -- swords, arrows, and any power that strikes them -- for sparring or a free-for-all. It only changes damage: area powers still aim past squadmates, and heals, shields, carries and buffs still treat them as friends. Everyone in the squad is told when it changes, the squad screen shows it, and it is saved with the squad. /squad friendlyfire off turns it back off; it is off for every new squad.
projecthero.guide.squads.pets: Pets (v0.15.11): a squadmate’s tamed animals -- wolves, cats, parrots, horses, Symbiote pet hosts and the rest -- are as safe from you as the squadmate is. Your sword, arrows and powers pass them by, and auto-aim never picks them. Only a rampaging Hulk ignores this.
projecthero.guide.squads.commands.body: /squad create <name> starts one and makes you its leader. /squad invite <player> offers a place; the offer stands for a minute and the invited player gets a clickable ACCEPT, or can type /squad accept. /squad leave walks away, /squad kick and /squad rename and /squad disband are the leader’s, and so is /squad friendlyfire on|off (plain /squad friendlyfire says how it is set). Plain /squad lists who is in yours. A squad holds up to 12, and survives a restart.
projecthero.guide.squads.menu.body: Press P at any time (P again closes it) for the squad panel, tinted in your squad's colour: the squad name, a crown if you lead it, how many are online, whether friendly fire is on (a red FRIENDLY FIRE ON tag) and a 12-slot capacity bar. Every squadmate has a card with their face, a tag in their current hero's colour, a smooth health bar (gold for absorption, a pulsing red edge when they are low), their coordinates, and how far away they are with a compass arrow that turns as you look around -- or the dimension they are in. Offline members are greyed out at the bottom; long squads scroll with the mouse wheel or arrow keys. The Commands tab (also shown when you are not in a squad) lists every /squad command -- click one to type it into chat. A button also toggles the Locator Bar: a thin hairline across the top of your screen with every online squadmate's face on it, sliding toward the middle as you turn to face them and growing larger the closer they are. The leader gets one more button, Friendly Fire, to switch it on or off.
projecthero.guide.zombie_raid.body: Somewhere out there is a Graveyard, and somewhere in the dark is a Cursed Zombie. Either one can make you Gravebound — and twenty minutes later, the dead come for you.
projecthero.guide.zombie_raid.curse.body: Twenty minutes of play. It survives logging out, dying, changing dimension, restarting the game, and milk. Only an Enchanted Golden Apple breaks it — everything else just delays the reckoning. While it runs you carry the Gravebound status effect: its icon and the time left show with your other effects (top-right of the screen and in your inventory).
projecthero.guide.zombie_raid.sources.bo: Activate the Cursed Grave in a Graveyard's crypt, or take a hit from a rare Cursed Zombie. Both lead to exactly the same curse: a second source never resets, extends or stacks your timer. Beating a Zombie Raid never makes you immune -- any time you are not already cursed, a Cursed Zombie can curse you again, and a used Cursed Grave rekindles after a minute or so.
projecthero.guide.zombie_raid.waves.body: Risen and baby zombies, Armoured Zombies that shrug off arrows, Acid Zombies that deny ground, Sword Skeletons that hunt archers, and Juggernauts that charge. Powered Zombie Bosses arrive on waves 4, 8 and 12, each carrying one of the mutations -- any of them, even ones you cannot get yourself yet.
projecthero.guide.zombie_raid.bosses.bod: An Empowered Zombie fights with a real mutation, not a bigger health bar: three to five of that power's current abilities -- a Laser Vision boss sweeps its beam and blasts you at close range, a Geokinesis boss races earth spikes at you and quakes the ground, a Super Speed boss blitzes and whips up a vortex. Its boss bar and nameplate name the power. Every big move is telegraphed (a wind-up, a ring on the ground, a charging sound) and its strongest one is saved for when it is badly hurt. It picks its targets -- whoever is hurting it most draws its attention (threat fades over about 10 seconds) -- follows fliers, closes on archers and goes for your pets too, but never harms its own horde. Kill one for a heap of Grave Essence and a chance at its head. The wave-12 boss always drops the Grave Champion Head.
projecthero.guide.zombie_raid.rewards.bo: Grave Essence from everything you kill; a Cursed Grave Chest after wave 12 with a pile of essence and — if you are lucky — a Gravekeeper Shield, a Necrotic Blade or an Undying Totem. Every Powered Zombie Boss also drops lapis, redstone, iron, gold, emeralds, amethyst and (from the middle waves on) diamonds -- more the later the wave, and the final boss adds golden apples, a lapis block and an enchanted book. The chest itself carries a full clear's haul of lapis (and lapis blocks), diamonds, gold, iron, redstone, emeralds, amethyst, golden apples and an enchanted book, with a chance of netherite scrap and ancient debris; a bigger party gets more (up to double for four or more). Your first clear also yields a Heart of the Grave.
projecthero.guide.zombie_raid.trophies.b: A boss's head is named for its power ("Geokinetic Zombie Head") and remembers who took it and on which day. Its eyes (and the Champion's crown gem) glow in the colour of the power's family. Wear it (shift-click it into the head slot, right-click the air, or let a dispenser put it on you) and it sits on your head like a mob head: an Empowered Zombie Head makes zombies notice you from half as far away, and the horned, crowned Grave Champion Head does that for every undead. Place it on the floor or mount it on a wall to build a trophy wall. Right-click a placed head to read its plaque. Breaking it keeps its power and record.
projecthero.guide.zombie_raid.crafting.b: Press four Grave Essence into a Gravebound Ingot. Two ingots and a stick forge a Necrotic Blade. Four ingots, four rotten flesh and a Totem of Undying make a Heart of the Grave — eat it and the next death that would kill you revives you like a held totem, once. The Oathbreaker drops the Broken Oath: put it in a Smithing Table with a Necrotic Blade and a Gravebound Ingot to make an Oathbound Necrotic Blade (13 attack damage, more Wither, 3 more kill stacks).
projecthero.guide.zombie_raid.repeat.bod: Raids are repeatable: get cursed again the ordinary way and the dead come again. Or take matters into your own hands -- craft the Heart of the Grave into a Grave Ritual Totem with Grave Essence, Soul Sand, Rotten Flesh and a Skeleton Skull, and use it in a Graveyard to curse yourself deliberately.
projecthero.guide.supervillain_raid.body: A rare assault on a village by one of three Supervillains and their raider army. It is not a vanilla raid and it does not happen often -- but it is never a one-off: beating one does nothing to stop the next.
Every so often a lone Pillager appears in the wild, sometimes with an escort, and heads for the nearest village. Look closely: the robe is darker, a faint purple particle drifts from it now and then, and its name shows on your crosshair. It is scouting for a Supervillain, and it is after you: it ignores villagers and leaves alone anyone it has already marked.
projecthero.guide.supervillain_raid.mark: Like Bad Omen: if the Spy's bolt hits you, or you kill the Spy, you get the Supervillain's Mark (100 minutes, milk clears it). Walk into a village with it and it becomes a 30-second Supervillain Omen, then the village is Marked for Attack. If a Supervillain Raid is already running there, you keep the mark until it is over. Nothing happens on Peaceful. An ordinary Pillager does nothing.
projecthero.guide.supervillain_raid.prep: Once the village is Marked for Attack, you have 10 minutes before the first wave. Warnings sound at 10, 5 and 1 minute and count down the final seconds. Use the time to build defences, protect the villagers, gather supplies, equip your gear and call for help. Leaving the village does not cancel the attack.
projecthero.guide.supervillain_raid.wave: Six waves. Waves 1-5 are escalating Pillagers, Vindicators, Witches, Evokers and Ravagers, each cleared before the next begins with 15 seconds to regroup. Wave 5 is the largest conventional wave — and then, after an ominous pause, wave 6 is the Supervillain itself. The raid bar counts all six, so "Wave 5 / 6" means there is still a boss to come.
projecthero.guide.supervillain_raid.vill: After wave 5 everything goes quiet. Then: SOMETHING POWERFUL IS APPROACHING. One of three villains arrives — the Chimera, the Arsenal or the Omega Mage — carrying a completely unpredictable superhero power, with a small escort. The appearance never tells you the power. Defeat the villain and the remaining raiders flee.
projecthero.guide.supervillain_raid.rewa: The Supervillain drops a large amount of experience, emeralds and a Villain Cache of high-level loot, and has a chance to drop a Supervillain Token, a Power Fragment of its power, and its unique trophy (Chimera Core, Arsenal Reactor or Omega Crystal). The victory also scatters lapis lazuli, redstone, iron, gold, diamonds, amethyst, golden apples and an enchanted book (a 30% lapis block, a 5% enchanted golden apple) -- more for a bigger party. Everyone who fought becomes Champion of the Village for 30 minutes — improved village trades.
projecthero.guide.titan.body: A very rare wilderness encounter, unrelated to the raid events above. Somewhere in the Overworld an ordinary-looking wanderer is not an ordinary zombie at all — kill it and the ground shakes as it rises again as a Titan: an eighteen-block giant that smashes terrain, throws boulders and does not stop chasing once it has seen you.
projecthero.guide.titan.tell.body: Look closely at a wanderer standing apart from a normal zombie horde: a faint yellow spark drifts off it every second or so. That is the only warning — it looks and fights like any other zombie right up until it dies.
projecthero.guide.titan.fight.body: Once it transforms there is no mistaking it -- a hunched, eighteen-block rotting giant with clawed, shackled hands, a torn-open ribcage and burning eyes: a boss bar, terrain-shaking footsteps and a fully animated set of telegraphed attacks, each on its own cooldown so it reads one move at a time. Every move winds up for two seconds and you can see which one is coming from its body. It notices from very far away and will run down a sprinting player, so come prepared before you kill the wanderer.
projecthero.guide.titan.rewards.body: Defeating the Titan drops a substantial reward for the fight it puts up. Losing costs nothing but the attempt — it only exists where a disguised wanderer happened to spawn, and killing it (intentionally or not) is what starts the encounter. It drops emeralds, diamonds, iron, lapis lazuli, redstone and gold, sometimes a lapis block, and a large amount of experience.
projecthero.guide.abyssal_behemoth.body: A very rare, endgame Nether world boss: an ancient, massively mutated Ghast, grown into a nine-block, floating apex predator crowned with obsidian horns. It is a genuine natural spawn — no summoning item, no altar, no command — and at most one exists in a Nether dimension at a time. 3,000 health.
projecthero.guide.abyssal_behemoth.fight: A boss bar, an Abyssal Core in its chest and a full nine attacks: Abyssal Fireball and Hellfire Barrage at range, Magma Rain and Netherstorm across the battlefield, a sweeping Abyssal Beam, Cinder Tether to pull it (and you) down to a low-altitude brawl, Hellwind and Sovereign Descent to punish standing underneath it, and Skyfall to punish staying too high above it for too long. Every attack telegraphs before it lands. Past 60% and 25% health it enters Netherfury and then Cataclysm — faster, angrier, shorter cooldowns — and staying in the fight for five straight minutes triggers Abyssal Enrage on top of that. You do not need flight: Sovereign Descent and Cinder Tether both force it down to your level with a real melee window. It turns on whoever is hurting it most: every hit builds threat that fades over about 10 seconds, so running away while a friend keeps hitting it no longer holds its attention.
It only spawns in large open Nether caverns, 48-128 blocks from a player, never on Peaceful — its ambient roar and the reddish glow of its core are usually audible and visible well before it notices you.
projecthero.guide.oathbreaker.body: A fallen death knight who broke his oath, his soul leaking out of him as soul fire. A three-phase duel boss in the Elden Ring mould: every attack has a readable wind-up, a window to dodge, and a recovery you can punish. He gets more desperate -- and less disciplined -- the lower his health drops.
projecthero.guide.oathbreaker.summon.bod: Craft a Knight's Soul (an Abyssal Core surrounded by 8 Grave Essence) and use it on a Respawn Anchor. The ground rumbles for five seconds, then he rises from a crouch. 4,000 health, plus 40% for every extra player within 48 blocks when he appears (up to four players); armour 10, toughness 4.
projecthero.guide.oathbreaker.poise.body: He can't be knocked out of his own swings, but every hit you land wears down a hidden poise meter -- even mid-wind-up. Deal about 400 damage without letting up for four seconds and he drops to one knee, sword planted, for 2.5 seconds: no attacks, and he takes 30% more damage. Stop hitting for four seconds and his poise comes back.
projecthero.guide.oathbreaker.phase1.bod: Disciplined, and relentless: he barely pauses between attacks and always turns to face you, so standing still will get you hit. Stance Dash (a long, glinting wind-up, then a lunge of up to 9 blocks that cuts everything it passes for 20 damage, then two seconds stuck in his stance -- punish it). He also uses it to close the gap when you back off. A four-hit combo from four directions, 7 damage a hit. The Oath Guard: if you've been hitting him, he may raise his sword before his face -- hit him from the front with melee and he parries with an anvil ring and ripostes you hard; hit him from behind, or with arrows, and it does nothing. He hops back if you crowd him, and if you keep your distance he leaps at you -- the landing spot is marked with a ring of soul fire, so get out of it. Stand behind him or crowd him and he answers with the Oathbound Whirlwind: the sword drawn low behind him, then two full spins that cut everything within 5 blocks -- back off or jump clear, then punish him while he reels, dizzy, for a second and a half.
projecthero.guide.oathbreaker.phase2.bod: At 60% he drives his sword into the ground: the oath shatters, a soul-fire shockwave throws everyone back, and soul-fire cracks split his armour. Everything from phase 1, plus: Soul Rend (he drags his sword behind him, soul particles mark a 12-block line, then it erupts -- step off the line), Chains of the Forsworn (a spectral chain thrown at range; if it catches you, you're yanked in for a strike; if it misses, he's wide open), a five-hit combo with unpredictable pauses before each strike, and a Stance Dash that sometimes feints first. Grave Geysers: he raises his sword two-handed and drives it into the ground -- a ring of soul particles appears under every player within 30 blocks, follows them for half a second, then locks, and a moment later a column of soul fire erupts there and throws whoever is standing in it into the air. Step off your ring once it locks; he stays bowed over his sword long enough to punish. Everything he does now hits 10% harder.
projecthero.guide.oathbreaker.phase3.bod: Below 25% he roars, his cracks split wider, and he runs you down. Judgement: he leaps high into the air, hangs there with a soul-fire beam pointing at where he'll land, then slams down -- the circle keeps burning for five seconds afterwards. Execution: a RED flash on his hand means an unblockable grab -- get out of the cone in front of him. If he catches you he lifts you up and impales you, unless the rest of your squad deals 150 damage to him first, which frees you and staggers him. A phantom of him also repeats his combo and dash swings a second after he makes them, so don't dodge once and walk straight back in. Everything he does now hits 25% harder.
projecthero.guide.oathbreaker.tells.body: A yellow-white glint means it can be dodged, or parried around. A red flash means it cannot be blocked at all -- move. Particles on the ground mark where something is about to land or erupt. Pillaring, swimming out of reach or hiding where he can't path gets a Soul Spear in phase 1 and the chains in phase 2 onward. He can find you from 50 blocks away, walls or no walls, and he turns on whoever is hurting him most: if a friend is only luring him, your hits will take his attention -- though he won't swap back and forth more often than every couple of seconds.
projecthero.guide.oathbreaker.rewards.bo: A netherite sword, 25-40 Grave Essence, a guaranteed Abyssal Core, the Broken Oath (a smithing template: with a Gravebound Ingot it turns a Necrotic Blade into an Oathbound Necrotic Blade -- 13 attack damage, more Wither, 3 more kill stacks) and a large amount of experience.
projecthero.guide.abyssal_behemoth.rewar: Defeating it drops its unique Abyssal Core along with netherite scrap, ghast tears, blaze rods and a 50% chance at ancient debris, plus a very large amount of experience. Both a natural spawn and a kill start a long cooldown before another can appear in that dimension.
projecthero.power.power_16_spider_climbi: Can be evolved into the Spider-Man Hero Class with an Arachnid Mutagen
item.projecthero.arachnid_mutagen.desc1: Refines an existing arachnid adaptation into something far greater.
item.projecthero.arachnid_mutagen.desc2: Useless to anyone who has not already been changed by a spider.
projecthero.spider_man.name: Spider-Man
projecthero.spider_man.desc: A Hero Class built entirely around movement. Swing across the sky, crawl over anything, and see trouble coming before it arrives.
projecthero.spider_man.ability.web_swing: Hold right-click with an empty hand to fire a web and swing from it; let go to release with all your momentum. Finds real anchors -- rooftops, cliffs, canopy, cave ceilings, your own webs -- and fires one high ahead of you when there is nothing to catch.
projecthero.spider_man.ability.web_zip.d: Fire at the surface you are looking at -- up to 100 blocks away -- and pull yourself to it, fast. Precision traversal: rooftops, ledges, the far side of a ravine, or a save on the way down. Hold sneak while zipping and you are hauled all the way to the block you aimed at. Zip webs fade out over 5 seconds and never stay stuck to your hand.
A thwip: a spinning glob of webbing flies where you aim and splats on what it hits -- 2 damage, 2 webbing, 0.3 s. Every hit is a stickiness stack (max 3): slowed, weakened and its jump weighed down for 18 seconds; three inside 3 s wrap an ordinary mob in a cocoon for 18 s. Puts fires out.
Line something and haul (50 blocks). An armed mob or player has its held items ripped out and flung to you; otherwise light things come to you, heavy things pull you to them, and dropped items come flying. 6 webbing, 1.5-second cooldown.
projecthero.spider_man.ability.wall_craw: Toggle. While on, touching any climbable surface in mid-air sticks you to it automatically -- no double-tap needed -- and sneaking locks you to that exact spot like a ladder rung. (Double-tap jump against a surface still works with it off.)
projecthero.spider_man.ability.web_net.d: Spin a temporary platform of webbing where you are aiming. A bridge, a floor, a landing pad or a trap. Dissolves on its own and puts back whatever it covered.
projecthero.spider_man.ability.web_strik: Web an enemy (30 blocks), get pulled in and land a three-punch combo: 5, 5, then a 9-damage finisher that knocks it back. 8 webbing, 2.5-second cooldown.
projecthero.spider_man.ability.web_throw: Combat Mode. HOLD the key to web a target and whirl it around your head; release to hurl it the way you are looking. 3 second cooldown. Bosses and immovable mobs are too heavy.
projecthero.spider_man.ability.impact_we: Hold R to charge (full after another second), release to fire one heavy ball: 10 damage (up to 15 fully charged), a hard knockback, and whatever it hits is cocooned for 18 s with a real cobweb where it is pinned -- knocked into a wall, it is pinned there. Fires by itself after 3 s. 12 webbing, 1.5-second cooldown.
projecthero.spider_man.ability.web_bloss: Hold V for 2 seconds, then leap and fire webbing in every direction: everything within 20 blocks takes 40 damage and is trapped for 18 seconds, and a ring of real cobwebs is left round where you stood. Let go early to cancel (nothing spent). 75 webbing, 20-second cooldown.
projecthero.spider_man.ability.trip_mine: Suit v2 only (replaces the Web Wall): stick a Trip Mine on the block you are looking at (within 5 blocks) or at your feet. It shines a thin web laser straight out up to 8 blocks; the first creature or enemy to cross it -- not you, not your squad, not a boss -- is yanked onto the mine and cocooned there for 25 seconds. Lasts 10 minutes; sneak + right-click picks it back up; 6 at once (a seventh replaces your oldest). 10 webbing, 2-second cooldown.
A ball of webbing that bursts where you aim (up to 30 blocks): everything within 4 blocks takes 3 damage and is rooted for 18 seconds, and real cobwebs fill the air round the splash for 18 s (they drop nothing and you and your squad walk through them). Squadmates are never caught. 15 webbing, 6-second cooldown.
projecthero.spider_man.ability.point_zip: Fire at the block you aim at (up to 100 blocks) and get hauled all the way to it. Aimed at a wall, you land on it already crawling (if your wall crawl is on); aimed at one of your tightropes or web strands, you land standing on top of it, balanced and facing along it -- even zipping up from below. 5 webbing, 0.5-second cooldown.
Hold G: zip at the enemy you aim at (30 blocks) and land a flying kick -- 14 damage and a huge knockback -- then bounce off it. 10 webbing, 5-second cooldown.
A rising uppercut on the enemy in front of you (5 blocks): 8 damage and it is launched skyward -- you leap after it. For 3 seconds every hit you land keeps it (and you) in the air. 6 webbing, 6-second cooldown.
projecthero.spider_man.ability.spider_co: Hold X: a one-second guard. The next attack -- a blow or a projectile -- is dodged with a back-flip and answered: 12 damage and a knockback to the attacker, and a projectile is sent straight back. 4 webbing; 8-second cooldown (3 if nothing came).
Spin a strand once round you: everything within 4 blocks takes 7 damage, is knocked away and stuck with webbing. 10 webbing, 4-second cooldown.
projecthero.spider_man.ability.grab_hurl: Web the mob you aim at (16 blocks), haul it to your hands and throw it: 10 damage when it hits something. With no mob, rip out the loose block you aim at -- not a chest or other block entity, nothing unbreakable or obsidian-hard -- and throw that: it shatters into its drops and hurts what it hits. Block grabbing obeys the server's config, terrain-damage setting, mobGriefing and land claims. 10 webbing, 5-second cooldown.
projecthero.spider_man.ability.swing_thr: Hold Z: web a mob (30 blocks) and whirl it round your head for as long as you hold; let go to hurl it the way you look -- 6 damage when it lands in something. Bosses are too heavy. 10 webbing, 3-second cooldown.
projecthero.spider_man.ability.tightrope: Press C on a surface for anchor A, then on a second surface within 40 blocks of it: a tightrope between the two. Either end can be fixed ON another of your tightropes or woven-web strands, so ropes join into networks -- walk across a junction and you carry straight on along the next rope; cut or fade a rope and the ropes hanging from it go too. Walk it perfectly balanced, Sneak to drop and hang under it (Jump flips you back on top, Sneak lets go), or swing from it. Aim at nothing to forget anchor A. 10 webbing.
A sticky 7 x 7 barrier 2.5 blocks in front of you. It stops every projectile not fired by you or your squad and traps mobs that walk into it; you and your squad can climb it. 25 webbing, 10-second cooldown.
projecthero.spider_man.ability.weave.des: Hold C, then left-click up to 10 surfaces (within 30 blocks, 8 webbing each) to place the anchors of the web; a marker shows the centre -- the middle of all your anchors -- with faint strands out to each. Let go of C: with 3 or more anchors the web is spun flat and even between them, radials from the centre and spiral threads in between (30 webbing) -- a huge spider-web across a ravine, a street or a room. With fewer than 3 it is cancelled and the webbing given back. You and your squad can walk on it, climb it and swing from it; anyone else sticks fast. 15-second cooldown; closes by itself after 30 s.
projecthero.spider_man.ability.spider_pu: Your Spider-Sense flares: every hostile within 32 blocks glows for you alone for 6 seconds, you get a burst of speed, and for 2 seconds every attack aimed at you is dodged. 10 webbing, 20-second cooldown.
projecthero.spider_man.ability.web_pin.d: Two presses. Shift+V on a creature or player within 24 blocks marks it: a web line hangs from your hand to it and it is outlined for you alone (not bosses, nothing too heavy to throw, not your squad). Then, within 6 seconds, Shift+V on a surface within 30 blocks -- a wall, the floor, a ceiling, or one of your tightropes or woven webs -- and it is reeled through the air and pinned there: back to the wall, standing on the floor, hanging under the ceiling, or with the strand through its chest. It stays cocooned for 25 seconds. Something in the way stops it short, cocooned where it hit. Shift+V on another creature marks that one instead; Shift+V on nothing drops the mark. 25 webbing, 3-second cooldown.
