advancement.projecthero.darkseid.apokoli: Defeat Darkseid without letting a single Mother Box overload
projecthero.guide.darkseid_raid.body: An endgame co-op raid for up to 8 heroes. Parademon waves, four Mother Boxes powering Darkseid’s shield, then three phases against the Lord of Apokolips himself. It never happens on its own -- you start it. Darkseid turns on whoever is hurting him most -- threat fades over about 10 seconds -- so the heroes dealing the damage draw his attention.
projecthero.guide.darkseid_raid.start.bo: Craft a Boom Tube Beacon (Nether Star, 4 Obsidian, 2 Echo Shards, 3 Crying Obsidian -- or a Nether Star with 4 Omega Shards and 4 Crying Obsidian) and use it. Every survival player within 48 blocks joins the roster (max 8). Others can join while Darkseid is above half health; after that the roster is sealed. The arena is 64 blocks across the beacon -- stray outside and you are warned, then pulled back after a few seconds. Flight is never disabled.
projecthero.guide.darkseid_raid.waves.bo: Five waves pour through Boom Tubes: Parademons; then Parademons with Ranged gunners (they strafe and circle you while they shoot, hover level with flyers and lead their shots); then Elites, Brutes and gunners in growing numbers for the last three. Parademons spread their wings and take to the air after flying heroes.
projecthero.guide.darkseid_raid.mother_b: Darkseid arrives shielded; four Mother Boxes around the arena each power 25% of the shield and he takes no damage until all four are down. Right-click a box and stay within 4 blocks for 10 seconds to disrupt it (hits do not interrupt you -- walking away, or his Grip, does). A box left alone for 90 seconds OVERLOADS: Darkseid heals, the box explodes, Parademons pour out and the ground burns. Even after the shield falls he calls them back: a minute or so after all four are dark, one or two power up again (you get a few seconds of warning) -- each takes 25% off the damage he takes until you disable it again.
projecthero.guide.darkseid_raid.phase1.b: Fists and a two-handed hammer up close; the Godly Ground Slam (the ring drawn on the ground is its reach -- it also hits flyers up to 10 blocks); OMEGA BEAMS, his favourite (you glow and get a warning -- two beams snake toward you in sharp zig-zags, then home in; blocks stop them and sharp turns make them overshoot); the Omega Barrage (warning circles where you are and where you are running -- leave them); DARKSEID’S GRIP (a purple line -- break line of sight before it closes; hitting him hard frees a gripped ally); the Omega Teleport (stay far away and he comes to you, even in the air); the Apokoliptian Charge (the lane is drawn on the ground -- step out of it); and Boom Tube reinforcements.
projecthero.guide.darkseid_raid.phase2.b: Faster, stronger, shorter cooldowns, more reinforcements, and the OMEGA BEAM SWEEP: a knee-high beam that turns a full circle around him. Jump it, fly over it, or put a block between you and him.
projecthero.guide.darkseid_raid.phase3.b: The arena burns and he is at his most dangerous (two sweep beams at once). About every 45 seconds he charges OMEGA ANNIHILATION on one hero for 5 seconds: the whole team must hit him hard (the boss bar shows how close you are) to interrupt it and stagger him for a big damage window. Fail and an arena-wide Omega blast hits everyone -- cover halves it, and it is worst for the marked hero.
projecthero.guide.darkseid_raid.death.bo: Dying does not end the raid: respawn and return after 25 seconds. The raid is lost only if every participant is down at the same time. After 15 minutes of fighting him he soft-enrages -- stronger every few minutes, more Parademons, and Mother Boxes switching back on (each takes 25% off the damage he takes until you disable it again).
Every official participant gets Darkseid’s Omega Core, likely 1-3 Omega Shards, a rare Mother Box (a personal Boom Tube home) and a very rare Omega Relic (24 charges of homing Omega Beams), plus a lot of experience. Each also gets a pile of Apokolips plunder: lapis and lapis blocks, diamonds, gold, iron, redstone, amethyst, emeralds, golden apples and two enchanted books, with a chance of netherite scrap, ancient debris and an enchanted golden apple (fewer invasion waves configured, less plunder). Advancements: Anti-Life, and Apokolips Falls for a raid with no overloads. Nobody gets Darkseid’s powers.
projecthero.guide.mutation.random_serums: Random-power serums (v0.13.18): the Mutagenic Serum grants a random Experimental power, the Heroic Serum a random Hero-Tier power, and the Prismatic Serum any power at all -- always one you do not have yet. A mutation needs a free mutation slot and replaces any hero power; a hero power replaces whatever you had. If nothing new can be granted, the serum is not used up.
message.projecthero.moon_knight.acquired: You who have fallen... Khonshu has chosen you. You are his fist.
Press H to wear the suit of Khonshu. R, G, X, Z, C and V hold his abilities (tap, hold, or with Sneak). Jump and hold Sneak to glide; hold right click to block with the cape.
message.projecthero.moon_knight.protecto: You protect those who travel at night (+%s Vengeance)
message.projecthero.moon_knight.resurrec: The full moon rises. Khonshu's favour returns to you.
message.projecthero.moon_knight.auto_sui: Khonshu will not let his fist fall -- the suit answers
message.projecthero.moon_knight.not_read: That move is still being forged
projecthero.guide.moon_knight.tier: Primary Power -- the Fist of Khonshu
projecthero.guide.moon_knight.body: Marc Spector died on an altar under the moon and came back as Khonshu's avenger. Moon Knight is a street-level hero who grows with the moon: strongest on a full moon night, weakest by day or underground, and fuelled by Vengeance for the ones who hunt the innocent.
projecthero.guide.moon_knight.origin.bod: Find a Temple of Khonshu in a desert (rarer than a desert pyramid). A hidden lower chamber holds the Scarab of Khonshu. At night, with the moon above the temple's open roof, right-click the altar with the Scarab, then stand on the altar and sneak -- kneel -- for 10 seconds while Khonshu speaks. Stop kneeling, step off or let the sun rise and the Scarab pops back out. Finish and you die in a flash of white... and rise again on the altar as his fist. Each altar only answers once. Sealed under a full moon, you begin with full Vengeance.
projecthero.guide.moon_knight.suit.body: Press H: for a second and a half white bandages spiral up your body and the suit materialises one pixel at a time (you can't be hurt while it does), then the suit of Khonshu is on, with its cape. While it is on you heal half a heart every quarter second, hit 7 harder with your fists, move 30% faster, jump clean over two blocks, walk straight up full blocks without jumping, and take 20% less damage -- and falls hurt you half as much again on top of that. Press H again and it dissolves away over another second and a half. The armour you were wearing is kept safe and handed back exactly as it was. Out of the suit, Khonshu will not let you fall: a single hit of more than 5 hearts, or being left under 4 hearts, starts the suit-up on its own (not in the 3 seconds after you take it off). The suit can't be taken off, dropped or stored, and none of Moon Knight's abilities or HUD work without it. While suited, his keys win over vanilla's creative hotbar save / load (C / X).
projecthero.guide.moon_knight.lunar.body: The moon has three states. Every ability's damage, range and duration is multiplied by it, and every cooldown divided by it: DAY x0.7 (the weakest), NIGHT x1.0 and FULL MOON x1.5 (the strongest). The numbers written on the abilities are the night numbers. The Nether and the End have no moon, so there it is always day. Any night -- ordinary or full moon -- also makes your darts home in, lets you call the Moonbeam, makes the Truncheon heal you and makes kills worth more Vengeance; only the full moon opens the Eye of Khonshu and recharges Khonshu's Resurrection. The HUD shows the state: the sun by day, tonight's moon at night, a glowing full moon under the full moon, with the multiplier beside it (hold Left Alt for its name).
A 0-100 meter. Killing a hostile mob that was hunting a villager, a wandering trader, an iron golem or another player gives +6; any other hostile kill gives +3 at night and +2 by day. Out of combat -- no damage dealt or taken for 5 seconds -- it regenerates on its own, 0.5% a second. Some abilities cost Vengeance. If it runs dry while you are suited your mind Fractures: another alter takes over for 20 seconds (it can only happen once every ten minutes).
projecthero.guide.moon_knight.alters.bod: Marc Spector, the fighter: +4 armour, +20% melee damage, harder to knock back. Steven Grant, the thinker: 15% less melee damage taken, extra loot from mobs, better prices from villagers, and every block he mines drops as if his tool had Fortune III (bare-handed too; a real Fortune tool never stacks with it -- the higher level counts). His Mr. Knight suit has no cape, so as Steven you can't Cape Glide or Cape Block. Jake Lockley, the shadow: faster while sneaking, mobs notice you from half as far away, +50% damage attacking from behind. Each wears his own suit -- Marc's white and gold armour, Steven's white, capeless Mr. Knight suit, Jake's dark suit -- and changing alter in the suit rematerialises the new one over the old, pixel by pixel.
projecthero.guide.moon_knight.resurrecti: While suited, the first fatal hit is cancelled: you rise at 6 hearts with a flash of white and a burst of crescents, untouchable for 2 seconds. It recharges only at the start of the next full moon night. The crescent on the HUD shows whether it is ready.
projecthero.guide.moon_knight.controls.b: Most keys have up to three moves: tap it, hold it, or press it while sneaking. The cape needs no key: jump and hold Sneak to glide, hold right click to block. They only work in the suit. Damage, durations and cooldowns below are night values: x0.7 by day, x1.5 under a full moon (cooldowns the other way round).
projecthero.guide.moon_knight.commands.b: Operators: /moonknight grant | revoke | vengeance <0-100> | locate_temple | moon <0-7> [day|night] | suit on|off | status.
projecthero.moon_knight.move.darts.desc: Throw a spinning crescent dart (15). At night it gently homes on a nearby hostile mob, and if it misses it curves back to you like a boomerang. Ready again after a second.
projecthero.moon_knight.move.dart_fan.de: Hold: five crescent darts fly at once, each locking on to one of the five closest hostile mobs you can see (within 32 blocks) and chasing it down -- 15 each, the same as a single dart. With fewer targets the spare darts double up on them; with none, they fan out ahead of you. 3.25 s cooldown.
projecthero.moon_knight.move.moon_mark.d: A dart that sticks in its target: it glows for 10 s and takes 30% more damage from you. 5 s cooldown.
projecthero.moon_knight.move.grapple.des: Fire a line up to 100 blocks. At a block you are pulled to it; at a mob, it is reeled in to you and stunned for 1.5 s (a boss is too heavy, so you are pulled to it instead). Hook a squad-mate -- or your own pet -- and you reel them in to you too: a rescue, no harm and no stun.
projecthero.moon_knight.move.dive_kick.d: Fire the line into an enemy up to 100 blocks away, get pulled in and crash into it feet first (20 + knockback). Forgiving aim: with nothing under the crosshair it locks on to the enemy nearest the crosshair (within about 9 degrees, in sight), and before you press it a ring of moonlight over that enemy's head -- and its name under your crosshair -- shows who you will hit. The pull chases and leads a moving target so the kick lands. Never locks on to your squad.
projecthero.moon_knight.move.yank.desc: Pull the mob you are looking at to you and stun it for 1.5 s.
projecthero.moon_knight.move.truncheon.d: Press C and the Truncheon of Khonshu appears in your hand at once (whatever you were holding slides into your inventory and goes back to that slot when you put it away). Tap C again to stow it. It hits for 7, and only exists while you are suited: drop it, store it or take the suit off and it is simply gone.
Hold C: the truncheon extends into a staff and you spin a full circle, hitting everything within 3.5 blocks for 15 and knocking it away. Brings the truncheon out first if it was not already.
projecthero.moon_knight.move.slam.desc: On the ground: a shockwave that hits everything within 4 blocks for 18 and throws it into the air. In the air: dive straight down and slam where you land -- 18 from six blocks up, more the further you fell (up to 36) -- and you take no fall damage.
projecthero.moon_knight.move.glide.desc: Jump, then hold Sneak in the air: you tip forward flat, the cape stretches between your arms and legs, and you fly like an elytra (no elytra needed, no fall damage): look down to dive and gain speed, pull up to climb on that speed (too long and you stall), level off to glide a long way, look left or right to turn. Glide into a mob to kick it (12). Let go of Sneak, or land, to stop. Not as Steven -- his suit has no cape.
projecthero.moon_knight.move.shroud.desc: Hold right click with an empty hand (or the Truncheon): the cape wraps around you and you take 30% less damage for as long as you hold it, but you move slowly. Not as Steven -- his suit has no cape.
projecthero.moon_knight.move.shadow_step: Blink 5 blocks backwards into a puff of shadow and vanish for 3 s.
projecthero.moon_knight.move.dash.desc: A burst of speed about 12 blocks exactly where you are aiming -- up, down or level -- with no fall damage at the end of it.
projecthero.moon_knight.move.alter.desc: Marc -> Steven -> Jake -> Marc. The new alter's suit rematerialises over the old one.
Open a small picker and choose an alter directly; let go to confirm.
projecthero.moon_knight.move.alter_speci: Marc -- Fist of Khonshu: Strength II and knockback resistance for 10 s (15 Vengeance). Steven -- Scholar's Sight: chests, ores and spawners within 16 blocks glow through walls for 8 s. Jake -- Vanish: invisible until you press Sneak+V again (or switch alter / take the suit off). No mob can target you while you are, not even one you strike -- everything hunting you loses track of you. The 20 s cooldown starts when you step back out.
projecthero.moon_knight.move.moonbeam.de: Call a beam of moonlight down on the block or mob you are looking at (up to 40 blocks). It hits every hostile within 4.5 blocks of where it lands: 35 at the centre, down to 21 at the edge, double to the undead -- never you or your squad. Night only; costs 10 Vengeance (10%); 5 s cooldown.
projecthero.moon_knight.move.eye.desc: The ultimate. Only under a full moon with 100 Vengeance: hold for 2 s. For one minute, every hostile mob within 30 blocks of you -- the area moves with you -- glows and is weakened (Weakness II) for as long as the Eye is open, you keep Strength II and Speed II, and every 2 seconds Khonshu brings a Moonbeam down on a random enemy near you (never your squad). Khonshu's skull looks down from the sky. Once per night.
projecthero.moon_knight.move.judgement.d: Judge the mob you are looking at (up to 32 blocks) for 15 s: it burns for 10 damage every second, and every point of damage you deal it while the Judgement lasts -- the burn and your own hits -- heals you. Costs 10 Vengeance (10%); 20 s cooldown.
item.projecthero.scarab_of_khonshu.desc1: A golden scarab bearing a silver crescent, cold as moonlight.
item.projecthero.scarab_of_khonshu.desc2: Lay it on the Altar of Khonshu beneath the night sky, then kneel upon the altar.
item.projecthero.scarab_of_khonshu.desc3: Found only in the hidden chamber of a Temple of Khonshu.

message.projecthero.khonshu.altar.holdin: The scarab glows. Stand upon the altar and kneel (sneak).
message.projecthero.khonshu.altar.spent_: The altar is cracked and silent. Its pact has been made.
message.projecthero.khonshu.refuse.spent: The altar is cracked and silent. Khonshu will not answer here again.
message.projecthero.khonshu.refuse.busy: A scarab already rests upon this altar.
message.projecthero.khonshu.refuse.day: The altar is dark. Khonshu answers only at night.
message.projecthero.khonshu.refuse.no_sk: The altar cannot see the sky. Khonshu cannot see you.
message.projecthero.khonshu.ritual.place: The scarab settles into the altar and begins to glow. Stand upon the altar and kneel.
message.projecthero.khonshu.ritual.wait: Stand upon the altar and kneel (sneak) before Khonshu.
message.projecthero.khonshu.ritual.line1: You who have fallen... do you hear me?
message.projecthero.khonshu.ritual.line2: The moon sees what others hide.
message.projecthero.khonshu.ritual.line3: I have watched you in the dark. You did not look away.
message.projecthero.khonshu.ritual.line4: Rise, and protect those who travel at night.
message.projecthero.khonshu.ritual.rise: Rise, my Moon Knight. The night is yours.
message.projecthero.khonshu.cancel.broke: You rose too soon. The scarab falls from the altar.
message.projecthero.khonshu.cancel.left: You turned away. The scarab falls from the altar.
message.projecthero.khonshu.cancel.dawn: Dawn breaks and the moon departs. The scarab falls from the altar.
message.projecthero.khonshu.cancel.no_sk: The sky is hidden. The scarab falls from the altar.
message.projecthero.khonshu.cancel.inter: The ritual was interrupted. The scarab falls from the altar.
advancement.projecthero.moon_knight.pact: Die on Khonshu's altar and rise again as the moon's avenger
projecthero.guide.structure.temple_of_kh: A rare sandstone temple found only in deserts, marked by a silver crescent over its door. Its roof is open to the moon above the Altar of Khonshu, and a hidden chamber beneath holds the Scarab of Khonshu. Lay the scarab on the altar at night and kneel to become Moon Knight.
message.projecthero.moon_knight.glide_ai: Jump or fall first -- the cape needs air under it
message.projecthero.moon_knight.yank_hea: Too heavy to reel in -- the line pulls you to it instead
message.projecthero.moon_knight.truncheo: Your inventory is full -- nowhere to put what you are holding
message.projecthero.moon_knight.alter_fr: The Fracture holds -- you cannot choose who you are right now
message.projecthero.moon_knight.scholars: Scholar's Sight: %s things worth knowing about nearby
message.projecthero.moon_knight.vanish: Jake slips into the shadows (%s lost your trail)

Nothing for the moonlight to fall on

The Eye of Khonshu needs full Vengeance (%s/100)

message.projecthero.gamma_serum.dosed: Gamma radiation burns through your veins...
message.projecthero.gamma_serum.dosed_hi: It is not enough on its own. Find a Gamma Reactor and right-click it -- if you dare.
message.projecthero.gamma_serum.already_: The Gamma Serum is already in your blood. Find a Gamma Reactor.
message.projecthero.gamma_reactor.not_do: The reactor hums. Without Gamma in your blood, touching the core would kill you.
message.projecthero.gamma_reactor.hulk: The reactor's glow makes your blood boil.
message.projecthero.gamma_reactor.surviv: You should be dead. Instead, something inside you is awake.
projecthero.guide.symbiote.passive.squad: Squadmates -- no Symbiote move touches a member of your squad: tendrils, spikes, the Onslaught and the resurrection blast pass them by, and their hits never cost the Symbiote Biomass.
projecthero.guide.symbiote.passive.pet: Symbiote Pet -- sneak + right-click your own tamed wolf or cat with an empty hand while suited to share the Symbiote with it (40 Biomass for a Normal host): it stays your pet, and whenever it fights it transforms -- black, bigger, stronger, with Latching Bite, Tendril Lash, Pounce, Spike Burst and a Guardian Shroud for you when you are low. Do it again to take the Symbiote back.
projecthero.guide.symbiote_spider_man.pa: The black suit is 15 armour with 1 toughness, and while it is on Spider-Man's own Resistance drops from II to I. Fire and sound always hurt it 50% more (double in Overdrive).
message.projecthero.combo.none: No combo: you need to own a matching pair of mutations.
message.projecthero.one_power_limit: Project Hero now allows one power at a time -- you keep your newest hero power.
projecthero.moon_knight.move.truncheon_c: Hits with the truncheon chain into a 3-hit combo: a forehand swing, a backhand (+3 damage and a shove), then a two-handed overhead smash (+6 damage and heavy knockback), and round again. Land each hit within 1.5 seconds of the last or it starts over; spam-clicking does not advance it. At night every hit on a mob heals you half a heart. The bonuses grow with the moon.
projecthero.guide.titan.moves.body: Punch: cocks its right fist back, then a turning haymaker. Backhand Sweep: winds one arm far out to the side, then sweeps it low across its front, hitting everyone in the arc. Stomp: lifts a knee high before bringing the foot down; get out from under it. Ground Slam: both fists raised overhead, then hammered into the ground. Shockwave: arms spread wide and raised, then a crouching blast that reaches 14 blocks. Grab: draws back an open hand, then snatches; it lifts you to its shoulder and hurls you. Boulder: scoops a rock out of the ground and heaves it overhead before throwing. Charge: lowers its head and paws the ground, then sprints. Leaping Slam (new): a deep crouch and a red ring on your spot; it jumps onto you, crushes whoever is under it, and a shockwave ring rolls outward from the landing. Jump as the ring reaches you to avoid it. Grave Roar (new): rears back drawing in souls, then roars. Everyone within 24 blocks is hurt, slowed and dragged toward it, and Husks claw their way up next to the group. It also swats anyone standing at its feet with a quick raised-arm chop.
projecthero.guide.titan.threat.body: The Titan does not lock onto one player any more. Every hit you land builds threat, standing close to it builds a little more, and threat fades over time. Every couple of seconds it turns on whoever is the biggest threat (sometimes someone close to that, to keep you guessing). A low growl and angry sparks over a player's head mark the switch. Its area attacks hit everyone in range, whoever it is chasing. Players in creative or spectator are ignored.
projecthero.guide.thor.perk.squad: Squad-safe: none of your lightning, shockwaves or hammer throws ever hurt, shove, slow or burn your squadmates or their pets
projecthero.guide.thor.perk.storm: Storm-Charged: while it is thundering where you stand, everything you hit hits 30% harder
message.projecthero.moon_knight.vanish_e: Jake steps out of the shadows
item.projecthero.unrefined_super_soldier: 10% it makes you a Super Soldier. 90% it kills you.
Refine it in a Blast Furnace (10 min).
item.projecthero.refined_super_soldier_s: Drink to become a Super Soldier.
message.projecthero.super_soldier.acquir: The serum takes. You are a Super Soldier.
R G Z X V (+Shift) are your moves; C throws a shield you hold. Shift+Z is your ultimate. Press P for details.
message.projecthero.super_soldier.title: SUPER SOLDIER
projecthero.super_soldier.ability.combo_: R: three fast punches on the enemy in front of you (5, 5, then a 7-damage finisher that knocks it back). Needs a target within 4 blocks. 5s cooldown.
projecthero.super_soldier.ability.upperc: Shift+R: a rising uppercut for 10 damage that launches the target about 5 blocks into the air. 8s cooldown.
projecthero.super_soldier.ability.shield: C: throw the shield in your hand. It bounces from enemy to enemy, then flies back to you. Adamantium Shield: 9 per hit, up to 4 enemies. Any other shield: 6 per hit, up to 3 enemies. Both fly up to 25 blocks. No cooldown: throw it again as soon as it is back in your hand.
projecthero.super_soldier.ability.leapin: Z: leap 4 blocks up and forward, then drive down into the ground: 12 damage to everything within 5 blocks (less at the edge), knocked back and up. No fall damage. 12s cooldown.
projecthero.super_soldier.ability.onslau: Shift+Z, ULTIMATE: a shockwave (8 damage, 6 blocks), then 10s of +5 melee damage, Resistance I, Speed I and +25% damage on every move. Every punch shocks enemies within 3 blocks of the target for 4. 100s cooldown.
projecthero.super_soldier.ability.tactic: X: a quick combat roll the way you are moving (or facing) -- about 5 blocks, and nothing can hurt you for half a second. 4s cooldown.
projecthero.super_soldier.ability.high_l: Shift+X: a huge leap -- 5 blocks up and far forward. No fall damage. 8s cooldown.
projecthero.super_soldier.ability.battle: V: rally the troops. You and squadmates within 16 blocks get Strength I and Speed I for 10s; hostile mobs within 12 blocks get Weakness for 8s and Slowness for 4s. 30s cooldown.
projecthero.super_soldier.ability.tactic: Shift+V: read the battlefield. Every enemy within 30 blocks glows for 10s, and for 8s every hit you land on a marked enemy is critical (x1.5). 25s cooldown.
hud.projecthero.super_soldier.title: Super Soldier
projecthero.guide.super_soldier.tier: Hero Tier -- a Primary power. Gaining it replaces the one you had.
projecthero.guide.super_soldier.body: Peak human, not a god: faster, tougher and stronger than any soldier, with a shield that always comes back. No transformation -- the power is always on.
projecthero.guide.super_soldier.serum.bo: Put one Potion of Strength, one of Swiftness and one of Leaping (long or strong versions work too) in a crafting table, any slots. Special recipe: it does not show in the recipe book. Drinking it is a gamble: 1 in 10 it takes, 9 in 10 your body rejects it and you die -- even in creative.
projecthero.guide.super_soldier.refine.b: Smelt the unrefined serum in a Blast Furnace for 10 minutes (keep it fuelled -- a lava bucket or a stack of coal). The Refined Serum always works.
projecthero.guide.super_soldier.passives: +50% movement speed, +5 hearts, +7 melee damage (bare-handed or holding anything, stacking with swords), 30% less damage taken, a 2-block jump and a longer safe fall, 20% knockback resistance, +15% attack speed, healing out of combat, and immunity to Poison and Nausea.
projecthero.guide.super_soldier.commands: /projecthero power grant super_soldier [player]  (op level 2). Every number lives in SuperSoldierConfig.
hud.projecthero.kryptonian.title: Kryptonian
message.projecthero.kryptonian.title: KRYPTONIAN
message.projecthero.kryptonian.subtitle: The yellow sun is yours
message.projecthero.kryptonian.acquired: The crystal pours stored sunlight into you. You are a Kryptonian.
message.projecthero.kryptonian.acquired_: Double-tap jump in the air to fly. R G Z X C V (and Shift+) are your powers. Stay away from kryptonite.
message.projecthero.kryptonian.fall: You drop out of the sky!
message.projecthero.meteor.streaks: A green-glowing meteor streaks across the sky...
message.projecthero.meteor.direction: It came down to the %s, about %s blocks away.
projecthero.kryptonian.ability.punch.des: R: one punch at whatever you look at (6 blocks) for 32, launching it along the punch, with a shockwave that hits everything within 3 blocks of it for 12. Punching thin air still flattens what is right in front of you (14). 5 Solar Energy, 3 s cooldown.
projecthero.kryptonian.ability.heat_visi: G, hold: twin red beams from your eyes, 32 blocks. 4 damage every quarter-second (16 a second) to whatever they touch, which bursts into flames; burns blocks when terrain damage is on. Animals it kills drop cooked meat. 1 Solar Energy a second while it burns, up to 10 s per burst, 3 s cooldown after you let go. The beams come out of your eyes in first and third person.
projecthero.kryptonian.ability.freeze_br: Z, hold: a stream of freezing breath in a 60-degree cone, 12 blocks: 5 damage every quarter-second, frozen solid and Slowness IV for 6 s. Water in its path ices over (it melts back), fires go out. 1 Solar Energy a second while you blow, up to 6 s per breath, 4 s cooldown after you let go.
projecthero.kryptonian.ability.thundercl: Shift+R: a clap that rolls out as a shockwave, an 80-degree cone 20 blocks long: up to 20 damage, thrown back hard and stunned (Slowness VII, Weakness II) for 2 s. 5 Solar Energy, 8 s cooldown.
projecthero.kryptonian.ability.ground_sl: Shift+G: on the ground, pound it; in the air, dive straight down and pound where you land (a longer dive hits harder). Everything within 7 blocks takes up to 30 and is thrown up and away; a small crater where terrain damage is on. 10 Solar Energy, 8 s cooldown.
projecthero.kryptonian.ability.solar_fla: Shift+Z, the ultimate: needs a FULL bar (100 Solar Energy) and spends all of it. Two seconds of the sun pouring out of you, then it all goes at once -- everything within 12 blocks takes 120, is thrown away and set on fire, and the ground caves in. Then you are powerless for 30 s: no powers, no flight, no Regeneration, no damage reduction and no Solar Energy -- and for the first 6 s Slowness IV, Blindness and Weakness IV. 90 s cooldown.
projecthero.kryptonian.ability.super_das: X: a blur of speed 28 blocks along your look (on foot it stays low), ramming everything in the way for 20 and knocking it aside. 3 Solar Energy, 3 s cooldown. In flight, X is Flight Boost instead: toggle it on and sprint flight goes from 45 to 55 blocks a second, with a sonic boom as you break into it. Free; it switches off when you land.
projecthero.kryptonian.ability.sky_launc: Shift+X: rocket straight up about 40 blocks (the take-off shockwave hits everything within 4 for 8) and hang there in flight. 3 Solar Energy, 6 s cooldown.
projecthero.kryptonian.ability.xray_visi: V: X-Ray Vision on or off. While it is on you see every living thing within 48 blocks outlined through walls, with night vision. Only you see the outlines -- nobody else gets them. Free, no cooldown.
projecthero.kryptonian.ability.super_gra: Shift+V: pick up the creature you look at (6 blocks; anything up to 4.5 blocks wide and players with PvP on -- never bosses or squad-mates) and carry it in front of you for as long as you like, even in flight. It cannot fight back or slip away, and the carry never hurts it. Shift+V again sets it down gently on the ground in front of you (no damage, no fall damage); V or attacking it hurls it instead -- it smashes into whatever it hits for 24, and 18 to everything around. Free; 4 s cooldown after a throw.
projecthero.guide.kryptonian.body: A Kryptonian under a yellow sun: nearly unbreakable, strong enough to launch a Warden with one punch, fast, fireproof, and able to fly. The sun is the fuel -- and kryptonite is the one thing that can bring you down.
projecthero.guide.kryptonian.origin.body: Somewhere out in the Overworld lies an old Kryptonite Meteor crater (see The Kryptonite Meteor) -- a rare find, like Mjolnir's crater. At the bottom of it sits the glowing Meteor Core, ringed with kryptonite ore. Mine the core with an iron pickaxe or better to get the green Kryptonian Crystal -- there is only one per crater. You can also craft one, but it is expensive: four enchanted golden apples in the corners, a block of kryptonite top and bottom, a block of diamond on each side and a nether star in the middle. Take it out under the open daytime sky and hold right-click: after two seconds it pours its stored sunlight into you. Like every Hero-Tier power it replaces whatever power you had.
Always on, no form to switch into: 40 max health (two rows of hearts), 80% less damage from everything that gets through (the same as Thor), and nothing at all from falls, lightning, fire, lava, drowning, suffocation or freezing. Bare fists hit for 15 with heavy knockback (more when sprinting), you cannot be knocked back yourself, you run 40% faster, jump about 4 blocks and step up whole blocks. Whenever you are hurt you heal 1 health every 2.5 seconds, paid for with 1 Solar Energy a second; it stops the moment you are back to full health (or the Solar Energy runs out). Direct sunlight keeps you fed. You never run out of air.
projecthero.guide.kryptonian.solar.body: The gold bar over your keys (0-100). It fills 6 a second in direct sunlight, 1.5 a second in daytime shade or rain, 0.75 a second at night and 0.375 a second underground or in the Nether and the End, all the time -- even straight after a move (v0.14.17: no more refill delay). Flying and your healing just slow the refill down while they run; only kryptonite stops it. The moves are cheap: 5 for the Punch, Thunderclap or Barrage, 10 for Ground Pound or Meteor Strike, 3 for the Dash or Sky Launch, 1 a second for Heat Vision and Freeze Breath. X-Ray Vision and Pick Up are free, flying costs 0.1 a second, and the Solar Flare takes the whole bar.
projecthero.guide.kryptonian.flight.body: Double-tap jump in the air to take off; double-tap again, or touch the ground, to land. You fly where you look: hold W to fly (look up to climb, down to dive), S to fly backwards, A and D to slide sideways, Space and Sneak to rise and sink. Let go of everything and you hover. You cruise at 20 blocks a second; sprint for super-speed flight -- 45 blocks a second. Press X in flight for Flight Boost: sprint flight at 55 blocks a second, and the sonic boom when you break into it (no boom otherwise). X again, or landing, turns it off. Flight costs 0.1 Solar Energy a second, so the bar does not refill while you are in the air; with an empty bar you drop out of the sky (the fall never hurts you) and cannot take off until it refills.
Kryptonite ore or a block of kryptonite within 5 blocks, a shard on the ground or in anyone's hand within 6 blocks, or a shard anywhere in your own inventory, and you are weakened: every passive switches off (so no damage reduction and no bonus health), you fall out of the sky, no move works, you get Weakness II and Slowness II, you lose 1 health and 5 Solar Energy a second, and your bar turns green. It passes 2 seconds after you get clear. Anyone can mine the ore (iron pickaxe) for shards -- and use them against you.
projecthero.guide.kryptonian.meteor.body: Meteors no longer fall out of the night sky (v0.14.13). Instead the Kryptonite Meteor is a rare crater generated with the world, about as rare as Mjolnir's crater and found in the same kinds of open land: a scorched bowl of blackstone, basalt and magma about 12 blocks across, kryptonite ore crusted round its centre (a few crystals sticking up) and one Meteor Core sunk into the middle. Explore new land to find one.
projecthero.guide.kryptonian.commands.bo: /projecthero power grant kryptonian [player] -- give the power. /projecthero meteor -- an operator can still call a meteor down near you; /projecthero meteor here -- one lands about 15 blocks in front of you. /projecthero power tune kryptonian solar <0-100> -- set your Solar Energy.

projecthero.guide.super_soldier.shield.b: Craft the Adamantium Shield: an iron block in each corner, a netherite ingot in the centre, red dye above it, blue dye below it and white dye either side. It blocks like any shield and never breaks. Hold it in either hand and press C to throw it; it comes back to the hand it left (or your inventory). Any ordinary shield can be thrown too, just weaker. If you die while it is in the air, it drops where it is.
projecthero.guide.super_soldier.suit.bod: A craftable four-piece Captain America suit (blue, red and white wool, iron and leather -- see the recipe book): 18 armour in all, between iron and diamond. Only a Super Soldier can wear it; anyone else finds it pops straight off.

projecthero.guide.hordes.body: Three craftable blocks that each hold a horde. Place one, right-click it in Survival, and the horde pours out of the block: eight waves that get bigger every time (18 mobs in the first, 60 in the last, and half again for every extra fighter -- several hundred in all), then a boss. Beat the boss and the block turns into a chest of loot.
projecthero.guide.hordes.rules.body: Everyone within 36 blocks of the block when it wakes is locked in, and anyone who walks in later joins the fight and is locked in too. A ring of coloured light marks the edge; walk past it and you are pulled back in. If you die, you have failed: you are out of the horde for good and cannot get back inside. When every fighter has fallen, the horde wins and its block crumbles to nothing. While a horde is running its block glows and cannot be mined. The sky darkens to the horde's colour over the arena.
projecthero.guide.hordes.zombie.body: Crafting: fill the crafting grid with rotten flesh. Zombies that do not burn in daylight (babies too, then armoured ones), husks, acid-spitting zombies from wave 3 and hulking Juggernauts from wave 5. Boss: a Titan -- the 18-block giant from the world event, with 1,000 health in a horde. Every horde boss gains health for each extra fighter; server owners can tune all of it in config/projecthero_horde.json.
projecthero.guide.hordes.skeleton.body: Crafting: fill the crafting grid with bone blocks. Skeletons and strays, bogged, sword and wither skeletons -- and six of the horde's own: small, pouncing Bone Runners; Blight Archers (Wither and Hunger arrows); Bone Knights in iron behind a shield no arrow gets past from the front; Bone Bombers with TNT heads and exploding arrows; Necromancers that raise the dead and heal the horde (kill them first); and hulking Bone Brutes whose Ground Slam you can see coming. They get tougher every wave. Boss: the Bone Tyrant, a seven-block lich-king with 1,200 health, stronger than the horde Titan -- greatsword sweeps, spike lines and spike rings (jump them), arrow volleys and storms, bone cages, a charge, Grave Step, and when enraged a sweeping soul-fire beam and a wither aura. Every move is telegraphed: watch his wind-up and the marks on the ground. The Bone Tyrant turns on whoever is hurting him most (threat fades over about 10 seconds), so one fighter cannot kite him while the rest hit for free.
projecthero.guide.hordes.spider.body: Crafting: fill the crafting grid with spider eyes. The hardest horde. Web-spitting Horde Spiders and cave spiders come first, then the brood: fast orange Hunters, green Venom Spitters that poison from range, purple Trapdoor Leapers (they crouch before they jump), yellow Acid Bursters (they hiss and swell when close -- back off or kill them from range), iron-plated Ironback Brutes, invisible Shadow Stalkers (only their eyes show, and their first bite hits double) and huge Broodmothers that burst into spiderlings when they die. Boss: the Brood Queen, a five-block spider queen with 1,400 health and three phases, each opened by a shriek that throws you back and darkens your sight. Watch her tells: she rears up before a Fang Lunge, a red ring marks a Leg Sweep or where a Leap Slam lands, her abdomen rises before a Web Volley (the centre web cocoons you) and pumps before Acid Rain (step off the bubbling marks), and it swells before an Egg Burst of spiderlings. From phase two she climbs a web line into the sky and drops onto the ring beneath her; in phase three she lunges three times in a row. The Brood Queen turns on whoever is hurting her most (threat fades over about 10 seconds), so one fighter cannot kite her while the rest hit for free.
projecthero.guide.hordes.rewards.body: Every chest holds diamonds, gold, iron, golden apples, emeralds and bottles of enchanting, and the harder the horde the more you get. Zombie: 3-6 diamonds, a 15% enchanted golden apple and an enchanted book. Skeleton: 5-9 diamonds, an enchanted bow, a stack of arrows, a 35% enchanted golden apple and a book. Spider: 8-14 diamonds, netherite scrap, a guaranteed enchanted golden apple (40% for two), a 50% totem of undying, a 30% block of diamond and two books. Every chest also holds lapis lazuli, redstone and amethyst shards: the Skeleton chest a 40% chance of lapis blocks, the Spider chest 2-4 lapis blocks and a 25% chance of ancient debris. More surviving fighters fill the chest further. Since v0.14.16 the loot is scattered through the whole chest in split stacks, like a dungeon chest. The horde bosses drop their own loot too: the Bone Tyrant bones, bone blocks, diamonds, emeralds, Grave Essence and a chance at a wither skeleton skull; the Brood Queen string, cobwebs, spider eyes, diamonds, emeralds and a chance at netherite scrap.
projecthero.guide.hordes.commands.body: /projecthero raid start zombie_horde|skeleton_horde|spider_horde -- place the block at your feet and wake it. /projecthero raid advancetimer <horde> -- skip to the next stage. /projecthero raid end <horde> -- stop it (the block goes back to sleep).
projecthero.guide.stark_sorter.body: A Stark-tech storage helper (v0.14.16). Fill its 54-slot store, press Sort, and a little red-and-gold Stark Sorter Bot launches from the pad and files everything away into the chests around it -- slowly enough that you can watch it work.
projecthero.guide.stark_sorter.recipe.bo: Top row: Gold Ingot, Basic Circuit, Gold Ingot. Middle row: Mechanical Part, Chest, Mechanical Part. Bottom row: Iron Ingot, Block of Redstone, Iron Ingot. Anyone can use it -- no power needed.
projecthero.guide.stark_sorter.use.body: Place it near your storage and right-click it. Put in the items you want filed and press Sort. The bot scans every chest, trapped chest and barrel within 10 blocks (a double chest counts as one), flies to each -- always facing the way it flies, carrying each load in its hands -- opens the lid and files up to 3 stacks per trip. When the station is empty it finishes the way Tidy does: anything in the wrong chest is carried over, and every chest is repacked and labelled. A packed station takes about a minute; the screen shows its progress.
projecthero.guide.stark_sorter.plan.body: The more containers it can reach, the finer it sorts. With 1-3 it uses four broad groups (Blocks / Tools & Combat / Food & Farming / Misc); with more it splits into up to 13 categories (Stone & Building, Wood, Decoration, Combat, Tools, Food, Farming & Plants, Ores & Minerals, Redstone, Mob Drops, Potions & Brewing, Project Hero Gear, Misc), and your biggest categories get extra chests. It keeps each chest's existing theme -- a chest that is mostly food stays the food chest -- and sends items to a chest already holding the same item first.
projecthero.guide.stark_sorter.safety.bo: Each category only ever goes into its own chests. When they fill up, the bot places a new chest from the supply next to them; if there is none, the rest stays in the station and the bot tells you how many chests to add. Nothing is ever lost or duplicated: breaking the station drops its store, its supply and whatever the bot was carrying, and if the bot is unloaded mid-job its cargo goes straight back into the station.
projecthero.guide.stark_sorter.tidy.body: Chests got jumbled? Press Tidy (under Sort). The bot works out what each chest is for from what it mostly holds -- the same rules as Sort, and an emptied chest keeps its old job -- then flies chest to chest, carrying anything in the wrong chest (up to 4 stacks a trip) to a chest of its own category. Every chest it opens is repacked: split stacks merged, everything moved to the front with no gaps, grouped by category and item. A big category may fill two chests, but it never strays into another category's chest. Pressing Tidy again on a tidy room changes nothing. The station's own store is not touched, and Tidy cannot start while a sort is running.
projecthero.guide.stark_sorter.supply.bo: The column on the right of the screen holds 3 stacks of signs and 3 stacks of chests. The bot hangs a waxed sign on each chest it opens -- "[Stark]" and the chest's category -- on the front if it is free, otherwise on a side, and re-writes its own signs when a chest's category changes. Signs you placed yourself are never touched, and a chest that has one gets no Stark sign. When a category runs out of room the bot places a chest from the supply in line with that category's chests (or on top of one, or beside the station). The column shows what is still missing -- "Add 3 signs", "Add 2 chests" -- and the bot tells you in chat when you press a button.

projecthero.guide.super_speed.origin.bod: The Speed Force is a second way to gain the Super Speed mutation, no serum needed. Get Strength, Speed and Jump Boost on you at the same time (potions, beacons, anything), then either activate a block of Charged Copper Plates within 4 blocks (right-click it or power it with redstone -- they turn up at Power Station research sites) or get struck by lightning (a thunderstorm, a channeling trident, a Thor). The surge always burns the three effects off: half the time the Speed Force takes you and you become a speedster, the other half it rejects you and you have to gather the effects again. It follows the mutation rules: with every mutation slot full nothing happens (you keep the effects), Super Speed replaces any other mutation or hero power you held, and gaining any other power later replaces it.
message.projecthero.power_wheel.none: No power wheel: it only switches between mutations, and you have none to switch
message.projecthero.speed.armour_tearing: Your armour is tearing apart at this speed -- only the Flash Suit can take Overdrive
projecthero.guide.flash_suit.body: A craftable four-piece suit only a speedster can wear. With all four pieces on, your Speed Mode and Overdrive SPRINT is 50% faster. It never speeds up your walking (v0.14.17), so moving around in it stays easy to control. It is the only armour that can take Overdrive -- any other armour loses 10 durability every second you run in Overdrive. Your after-images wear whatever armour you have on. Diamond-strong (3/8/6/3 armour, 2 toughness), no other powers. Press H while wearing it: the suit is pulled back into a gold Flash Ring on your right hand. Press H again: the ring snaps open, the compressed suit shoots out and swells, and you whirl into it in a storm of lightning as it spreads over you from the ring. While it holds the suit, the ring is worn in your CHESTPLATE slot (the slot the Flash chestplate leaves free), so it is treated exactly like armour: kept with keepInventory, and on death it drops with the rest of your gear and never despawns -- the suit is never lost. Right-click it (or put it in the chest slot) to wear it again. The ring shows on the knuckles of your right hand (body side, and in first person) only while the suit is packed inside it, and while it is in there the suit slowly mends itself (1 durability per piece every second) -- the line just above your Super Speed HUD shows how far along it is ("Suit 87%": the durability left across every packed piece; yellow at half, red at a quarter). Crafting (R red wool, D diamond, G gold ingot, S sugar, L lightning rod): Cowl RDR / G G, Chestplate R R / DLD / RSR, Leggings RDR / S S / R R, Boots D D / G G.
projecthero.guide.kryptonian.suit.body: A three-piece armour set (chestplate, leggings, boots -- no helmet, so your own face and hat layer show) only a Kryptonian can wear -- anyone else cannot put it on, and if you lose the power while wearing it, it slips off into your inventory. Netherite-strong (8/6/3 armour, 3 toughness, a little knockback resistance) and fireproof, but it grants no powers. Like you, it feeds on the sun: standing in direct sunlight, every piece you wear slowly mends itself (1 durability per piece every second). The chestplate brings a red cloth cape with the gold shield on the back: it sways as you walk and streams out behind you in flight, lying almost flat at super-speed. Crafting (no kryptonite!): Chestplate -- two red wool, two diamonds and a block of gold, three blue wool. Leggings -- gold ingot, red wool, gold ingot over two blue wool and two diamonds. Boots -- two red wool over two diamonds. Each piece you wear also lets you soak up more sunlight: the full suit fills your Solar Energy 50% faster.

projecthero.guide.syndicate.body: A street-level raid on the Kingpin's crew - the first boss fight that needs no powers, between the Zombie Horde and the Supervillain Raid.
projecthero.guide.syndicate.start.body: Craft a Police Scanner (compass, iron, redstone) and use it. It picks up chatter about a Syndicate warehouse 60-110 blocks away and the warehouse is there. Hold the scanner to follow its bearing. Walk inside, or up to the roller door, and the bust begins. It needs open, dry, fairly flat ground and never runs on Peaceful.
projecthero.guide.syndicate.waves.body: The crew comes through the roller door and side doors, and early on out of the back room under the mezzanine. Every wave is bigger and better armed, and grows by half for each extra player. Use the crates for cover.
projecthero.guide.syndicate.crew.body: Thugs swing clubs, crowbars and knives. Pistol gunmen keep their distance and strafe, then reload - push them while they do. Shotgunners walk straight at you. Snipers hold the catwalk and paint you with a red laser for a second and a half before firing: break line of sight. Enforcers charge shoulder-first; dodge so they hit a wall and they are dazed and take extra damage. A raised shield blocks bullets.
projecthero.guide.syndicate.kingpin.body: He walks out of his office on the mezzanine. Watch for the Bull Rush wind-up (he lowers his head and the floor shakes) and make him run into a wall - he is stunned and takes half again as much damage. Up close he grabs and throws; hit him hard while he holds someone and he drops them. Far off, his cane fires three shots. He whistles for more crooks at two-thirds and one-third health, and enrages at 30%. His suit takes a quarter less from projectiles. He turns on whoever is hurting him most: every hit builds threat that fades over about 10 seconds, so running away while a friend keeps hitting him no longer holds his attention.
projecthero.guide.syndicate.rewards.body: Beat him and the stash in his office becomes a chest: a Villain Dossier for every fighter (read it to take the Supervillain's Mark and bring on a Supervillain Raid), the Kingpin's Cane (a heavy club with a hidden barrel), Punisher ammunition and gun parts, emeralds, gold, diamonds, redstone and more. Lose, and the crew clears out; the warehouse stays for another try.
projecthero.guide.syndicate.commands.bod: /projecthero raid start syndicate builds a warehouse in front of you and starts the bust. end stops it, advancetimer skips to the next stage.

projecthero.guide.crime.body: Small, everyday crimes that happen on their own near villages - no powers needed, any player can step in.
projecthero.guide.crime.when.body: Spend time within about 96 blocks of a village bell and every 10-20 minutes something happens there (each player and each village has a cooldown). Never on Peaceful, and never during a raid or another event in the same area.
projecthero.guide.crime.alerts.body: Everyone within 96 blocks hears a scream from the crime's direction and gets a chat line, a red bar at the top of the screen and a "~40 m NE" hint above the hotbar. The village bell rings, and villagers who hear it run indoors.
projecthero.guide.crime.mugging.body: One to three thugs corner a villager. The bar shows how much more the villager can take. The thugs only turn on you when you hit them or get within 6 blocks. Put them all down before the villager is knocked out; if it is, it can't move for a while but recovers.
projecthero.guide.crime.break_in.body: Two to four crooks walk in, rob a house chest (or the bell square) and run with a loot sack each. They never fight back. Put down a crook carrying a sack and the goods spill out. Stop at least as many as get away. The sacks are the crooks' haul - nothing is taken from real chests.
projecthero.guide.crime.getaway.body: A crook loads up at the bell square while one or two pistol gunmen cover him, then sprints for the edge of the village. A sprinting player is a little faster than he is. Put him down before he is 80 blocks out. Hitting him early starts the run early.
projecthero.guide.crime.arson.body: A firebug wanders the streets lighting small fires, only on bare ground away from anything that burns. Stop him before he lights eight, then put out what is still burning. All his fires go out when it ends.
projecthero.guide.crime.rewards.body: Everyone who hurt a crook gets emeralds, iron ingots, some food and experience, and the villagers think better of them. Whoever did the most also gets Hero of the Village for three minutes (cheaper trades). Fail, and nothing worse happens than the crooks getting away.
projecthero.guide.city.body: A City is a very rare, very large village that kept on growing: about 240 blocks across, a real village at its edge, a town of cobble lanes and townhouses, and a downtown of avenues and towers in the middle. Villagers live, work and gather there as in any village.
projecthero.guide.city.finding.body: Cities generate in plains, sunflower plains, meadows and savannas, on fairly flat, dry ground, and never right next to an ordinary village - roughly one per 2,500-block region. Journeyman cartographers sell a City Map (emeralds and a compass) marking the nearest one, and /locate structure projecthero:city finds one too.
projecthero.guide.city.rings.body: Downtown: asphalt avenues, sidewalks, street lights and the tall buildings. The town: cobble lanes, townhouse rows with back gardens, and the civic buildings. The village edge: a packed-earth ring road lined with village houses. Like a village, it follows the land: the roads hug the ground and the buildings get foundations.
projecthero.guide.city.downtown.body: Four city blocks around the central crossing: the Police Precinct and the Office Tower with the City Bank behind them, the Hospital and an Apartment Tower, the Daily Bulletin and the Clock Tower, and the Train Station. The courtyards between them are small gardens.
projecthero.guide.city.town.body: Every City has a Market Square with a mall and six trade stalls, a Central Park with a fountain and a hero statue, a Fire Station and a Maintenance Depot. Around them: townhouse rows, brownstone walk-ups with roof gardens, a construction site, the docks and little pocket parks.
projecthero.guide.city.village.body: The ring road is where the City turns back into a village: the houses and side streets along its outside are real village buildings, plains or savanna to match the land.
projecthero.guide.city.villagers.body: Villagers arrive with the buildings and claim the job sites: lecterns in the offices, bank and newspaper, cartography tables in the office tower and station, brewing stands in the hospital, cauldrons in the fire station, the six market stalls and every townhouse workshop. They sleep in the flats, townhouses and walk-ups and meet at the market, park and clock tower bells. Iron golems guard the squares, and raids work as in any village.
projecthero.guide.crime.commands.body: /projecthero crime start <mugging|break_in|getaway|arson> starts one at the nearest village (or in front of you). end stops them all, trigger rolls a natural one now, status lists them. Frequency, kinds and rewards are in config/projecthero_crime.json.

gamerule.projectheroCityRepair: City Repair Workers rebuild City damage
projecthero.guide.city_services.body: A City looks after itself: Repair Workers rebuild what fights break, City Cops patrol, doctors heal, firefighters put out fires, the bank keeps your emeralds and the newspaper tells you where trouble is.
projecthero.guide.city_services.repair.b: Break a City building and the damage is noted. 10 minutes after the last damage in an area, during work hours, a Repair Worker (hi-vis vest, hard hat) walks out of the Maintenance Depot and rebuilds it bottom-up, one block every half second, climbing scaffolding for high spots. He works holes from their rim, never from inside, and lifts any villager or animal out of a hole before he closes it (if you are standing in it, he leaves that bit until you move). Up to 512 blocks a trip. With no worker left, the depot hires one each day, and damage slowly fills in on its own.
projecthero.guide.city_services.repair_r: Only empty spots (air, water, lava or fire) are refilled. Your own blocks are never replaced: build in a damaged spot and that corner of the City is yours from then on. Chests and other containers come back empty, the bank vault's treasure comes back as stone bricks, and a rebuilt block drops nothing if broken within a day.
projecthero.guide.city_services.food_ban: The crate of produce in the Market Square. Villagers with more food than they need (mostly farmers) carry the rest over in the daytime, and you can use food on it too. Every 60 food (12 bread) becomes a newborn villager - at most one an hour, only while a bed nearby is free, and never during a raid. Craft one (barrel + hay bale + bread) to grow any village. Use it empty-handed to see its stock.
projecthero.guide.city_services.cops.bod: Villagers who work a Precinct Desk. Tougher than other villagers (40 health, armour, a baton), they patrol near the precinct, fight monsters, and answer crimes nearby - though they only join a crime after 20 seconds and hit crooks softly, so you still matter. They never attack players unless you hit them first. Use the desk to read the crime reports.
projecthero.guide.city_services.doctor.b: Clerics working in the City hospital are doctors. Inside the hospital you get Regeneration II. Doctors throw a Healing potion at hurt players and villagers nearby once a minute, and sneak + use a doctor holding 2 emeralds for a full heal that also cures poison, wither and hunger.
projecthero.guide.city_services.firefigh: Leatherworkers working in the City fire station are firefighters. When something burns in the City they run to it and put the fire out, one block every half second.
projecthero.guide.city_services.bank.bod: A Safe Deposit is your own emerald vault - every Safe Deposit opens the same account, and only emeralds and emerald blocks fit. It pays 1% a day, added when you next open it, up to 64 emeralds of interest in total.
projecthero.guide.city_services.bulletin: Librarians at the newspaper office sell it for an emerald. Read it for today's crimes, raids and world events within 1000 blocks, nearest first, with directions from where you stand. It is reprinted every time you open it.
projecthero.guide.city_services.commands: /projecthero city status | repair (send a worker now) | sweep | optout <radius> | reset <radius>. The gamerule projectheroCityRepair turns repairs off. Numbers are in config/projecthero_city.json.
projecthero.guide.carnage.body: The Symbiote's red, insane offspring - a world boss that falls from the night sky. 1000 health for one fighter (+250 for each extra, up to 3500), armour as tough as a full iron set, and he regenerates 2 health every 2 seconds. Symbiote hosts draw him four times as often.
projecthero.guide.carnage.arrival.body: On Overworld nights a crimson meteor may streak down near a player. Carnage climbs out of the impact a few seconds later. Only one roams a world at a time.
projecthero.guide.carnage.moves.body: Blade-arm combos up close, a leaping pounce from range, crimson tendrils that whip and drag everyone within ten blocks, and fans of crimson spikes. He picks a ready move at random and takes a short breather after each one. He turns on whoever is hurting him most: every hit builds threat that fades over about 10 seconds, so running away while a friend keeps hitting him no longer holds his attention.
projecthero.guide.carnage.new_moves.body: Tendril Whip Sweep: two long tendrils rear up behind his right shoulder, then whip across everything in front of him out to 8 blocks - get behind him or out of reach. Axe-Arm Cleave: his arm grows into a huge crimson axe and he leaps at you; the landing spot glows red, and a ring of shards races out from the impact - jump it or be clear. Spike Eruption: he punches the ground and glowing red cracks run toward you - step off them before the spikes burst up. Symbiote Snare: a glob of goo swells in his fist and is lobbed at you; it roots whoever it splashes in a tendril cocoon for 2 seconds.
projecthero.guide.carnage.split.body: At three-quarters, half and a quarter health he wraps himself in an untouchable cocoon and releases a brood of Crimson Spawn. Kill them all and he bursts out reeling, taking half again as much damage. Leave them for 20 seconds and they crawl back in and heal him. After the third split he frenzies.
projecthero.guide.carnage.weakness.body: Fire does double damage, makes him flinch and stops his regeneration for 6 seconds. Sound breaks him: ring a bell or blow a goat horn near him and he writhes helplessly, taking half again as much damage. Explosions hurt him more.
projecthero.guide.carnage.rewards.body: He drops Crimson Biomass - more for a bigger party. A Symbiote host can absorb it: Biomass fully restored and a minute of crimson frenzy (Strength II, Speed, Regeneration).
projecthero.guide.carnage.commands.body: /projecthero raid start carnage drops a meteor beside you; end removes him. Spawn tuning lives in config/projecthero_carnage.json.
screen.projecthero.ironman_info.flight_f: Free flight (double-tap jump; sprint needs the chestplate)
screen.projecthero.ironman_info.hint: Scroll to read more. Press I or Esc to close.
projecthero.guide.iron_man.scanner.body: Every helmet but the Mk I reads out whatever is under your crosshair with the visor closed: name, health, armour, distance and threat. The Mk VI Suitcase reaches 25 blocks, every other suit 100. Lift the faceplate and the whole HUD goes dark.
projecthero.guide.iron_man.targeting.bod: The Mk VI Suitcase and Mk III lock onto whatever is right under your crosshair, or else the hostile nearest it (a gold and red reticle marks it), and switch the moment you aim at a different creature, so you can pick one out of a group. Locked, they auto-aim: repulsors, the Unibeam, rockets and missiles go straight to it.
projecthero.guide.iron_man.spec_sheet.bo: Press I while wearing any Iron Man piece for the suit's spec sheet: energy, integrity and repair rates, flight, weapon damage, every ability and the helmet systems.
projecthero.guide.iron_man.auto_feed.bod: Every suit from the Mk III up feeds you from your inventory when you are hungry enough not to waste it -- any safe food, modded food included, and bowls and bottles come back. It never touches raw meat or fish, food with side effects (rotten flesh, spider eyes, pufferfish), chorus fruit, suspicious stew or golden apples. The Mk I and the Mk VI Suitcase don't feed you.
projecthero.guide.iron_man.furnaces.body: Upgrade a furnace, blast furnace or smoker with iron, gold and redstone around it. The Stark Furnace cooks one item every 2.5 seconds; the Stark Smelter (ores and metal gear) and the Stark Smoker (food) one every second.
projecthero.guide.iron_man.mark_1.body: Grey scrap iron, built in a cave: slow (walks 10% slower), no flight -- it rocket-jumps instead -- but it hits the hardest of Era I. Integrity 700, absorbs 30%, reactor 600 (1 a second). Moves:
projecthero.guide.iron_man.mark_2.body: The classic red and gold, carried in the Briefcase (C or right-click the case: it drops, flips open and the suit climbs on boots first; hold Shift+C to fold it back into the case in your hand). 1000 integrity, absorbs 30%; 3/8/6/3, toughness 2.5; flies 18 (28); +7 melee; lock-on; breathes underwater. R Repulsor -- tap 11, hold 1 s and release for a charged 20 / Shift Dash (16). G Tractor Beam (hold: lift a target on a beam, release to throw it) / Shift Pressor Blast (cone shove, 10). X Flares / Shift Supersonic Boost (20 s). Z round Unibeam (26, pierces) / Shift Unibeam Flash (short-range stun burst, 8). V Wrist Laser (a thin red cutting beam: 18 + fire to up to 3 enemies in a line) / Shift JARVIS Scan (scanned enemies take +25% for 15 s). C Mob Highlight; hold Shift+C folds it into the case. Reactor (v0.16.7): 1400 energy, +2.5/s; every move costs energy and flight drains 2/s (4 sprinting); at 0 the suit browns out until 10% is back.
projecthero.guide.iron_man.mark_iii.body: The iconic red and gold (the comic Armor Model 4): real flight (it drains the reactor), the chest unibeam and good all-round stats. Integrity 1400, absorbs 38%, reactor 1200 (2 a second). Moves:
projecthero.guide.iron_man.platform.body: Any suit docked on a Suit Platform repairs 5 integrity every second, while two welding arms rise out of the pad and spark over the plates until it is whole. Suits have no energy any more, so docking is purely repair (the Mk VII and Mk VIII also repair themselves out of combat). Build a Stark Gantry Floor within 20 blocks and its arms put the suit on and take it off (see Stark Gantry). Sneak + right-click the platform with the Mk VI Briefcase in your pack to unfold the Mk VI onto the rack; with a Mk VI racked, the Briefcase tab beside the platform screen folds it back into its case.
projecthero.guide.iron_man.gantry.body: Craft Stark Gantry Floor (Metal Plating, Piston, Metal Plating / Mechanical Parts, Basic Circuit, Mechanical Parts / Metal Plating, Piston, Metal Plating -- makes 8) and lay a complete 5 x 5. Stand anywhere on it as Tony Stark and press H: a menu lists every suit racked on a Suit Platform within 20 blocks of the floor, with its charge, integrity and distance. Pick one and the whole suit leaves its platform: the centre lifts you half a block, the floor slides open to your left, right and front, two robotic arms rise out of it and the suit goes on part by part, to a beat, while the camera swings round so you can watch: the top half of the chestplate first, 1 s later the right gauntlet and 1 s after it the left (one arm each), 1 s later the right boot and 1 s after it the left, 1 s later the leggings, 1 s later the helmet and 1 s later the faceplate. The parts that build themselves on start the moment the part they grow from is fitted and keep building while the arms work on. In detail: the arms fit the top half of the chestplate, the bottom half builds itself down from it and the outer layer builds over it; each gauntlet is fitted (right, then left), the rest of the arm builds up from it and the sleeve layer over it; the boots go on one at a time (right, then left), each by its own arm, then the top half of the leggings, the bottom half builds down and the pant-leg layer over the legs and boots; last the helmet, and its faceplate on its own -- then everything sinks back and the floor closes (about 12.5 s for a full suit; the newest Mark is at the top of the menu). You are held still and can't be hurt while it suits you up. Press H on the gantry in a suit and choose Remove Suit or Swap Suit (arrows + Enter, or R / S; Esc cancels). Remove Suit is exactly the same in reverse -- faceplate first (the HUD and the mob highlight go dark the moment it lifts away, and come on the moment it is fitted when suiting up), every built layer taken apart -- the pieces lowered into the floor and racked on the platform they came from (or the nearest one in range with room). Swap Suit lists every other suit (racked in range or carried in your pack): pick one and the gantry takes your suit off as above, sends it home (its own platform, else the nearest one with room, else your pack) and straight away puts the new one on, in one sequence -- if the suit you picked was taken meanwhile, you just end up unsuited. Suits carried in your pack are listed beside the racked ones, and go back into the pack if cancelled. Sneak cancels any of these -- nothing is ever lost: pieces still in the floor go back to a platform (or your pack). Shift + H on the gantry still opens the faceplate.
message.projecthero.ironman.mk5_packed: The Mk VI pieces fold into a briefcase. Press C or right-click the case to suit up.
screen.projecthero.suit_call.remote_pilo: Remote Pilot: deploy this suit as a drone and fly it from where you stand. Your body stays behind, unprotected, and any hit on it drops the link. Range 96 blocks. C ends the link and the suit flies home.

message.projecthero.ironman.orbital_fall: The pod could not reach you. Suiting up from your pack.
projecthero.guide.iron_man.mark_6.body: The SILVER CENTURION. 2200 integrity, absorbs 45%; 4/9/7/4, toughness 3.5; flies 22 (38); +9 melee; Resistance I; repairs 8 integrity/s after 10 s out of combat. R Repulsor (17) / Shift Dash (22). G Pulse Bolts (10) / Shift Pulse Storm (8 rapid bolts). X Ricochet Repulsor (20, bounces through 4) / Shift Chameleon Effect (6 s invisible). Z Heavy Triangular Unibeam (40) / Shift Unibeam Overcharge (charges 1.5 s, then 75). V Deploy Blades (thin silver blades slide out of both gauntlets: +6 melee and every hit sweeps the enemies round the target; V again to retract; 10 energy, then 1 a second) / Shift Blade Whirl (a lunge and two spinning slashes, 16 each, 4.5 blocks; deploys the blades). C Energy Shield (6 s, stops 80%); hold C 1 s for the Overload Burst (30 all round); hold Shift+C folds it into its backpack. Reactor (v0.16.7): 1800 energy, +2.5/s, flight 2/s.
projecthero.guide.iron_man.mark_8.body: The HULKBUSTER -- about 3 blocks tall, drawn as its own segmented body (first person: its huge forearms). 4500 integrity, absorbs 60%; 5/10/8/5, toughness 5; a slow jet-hover at 10 b/s; +16 melee; knockback immune; x1.5 damage on bosses and the Hulk; never repairs itself except by its Replacement Pod. C Hydraulic Brace, hold C 1 s for Sentry Mode; called with the Stark Glasses it drops in from orbit. R Giant Punch Combo (a jab, a hook and an uppercut finisher: 26, 26, 38) / Shift Rocket Fist (the right forearm flies off, hits for 45 and flies back). G Pile-Driver Slam (40 around you) / Shift Earthquake Stomp (a shockwave 18 blocks ahead, 32 + launch). X Grab & Pound (2 x 20) / Shift Grab & Throw (18 + 18 on impact). Z Chest Mega-Beam (the chest opens, then 5 pulses of 18) / Shift Shoulder Missile Swarm (10 x 18). V Palm Cannon (both palms fire one heavy blast each: 22 + a 3-block splash of 10) / Shift Replacement Pod (an orbital pod restores 30% integrity, 3 min cooldown; works even on a disabled suit). C Hydraulic Brace (5 s, 70% less damage); hold C 1 s for Sentry Mode. Reactor (v0.16.7): 2500 energy, +2.5/s, hover 2/s; the pod and Sentry Mode work on a dead reactor. Touching down after flight (or a big fall) it lands like a superhero: a hard landing slams down onto one knee and a fist with a ground shock, a gentle one just soaks it up in the knees; move after the impact to walk straight out of it. Suiting up -- the mid-air build or stepping in -- each piece brings half of its plating and the rest slides out from under it before the outer plates build on.
projecthero.guide.iron_man.mark_vii.body: The SPACE armour. 2600 integrity, absorbs 50%; 4/9/7/4, toughness 4; the fastest flier, 24 (44), no altitude ceiling; immune to fire, lava and freezing; +9 melee; repairs 15/s after 10 s out of combat; still called with the Colantotte Bracelets / orbital pod. R Repulsor (20) / Shift Dash (25). G Vacuum Micro-missiles (6 x 20, each blast sucks enemies in) / Shift Orbital Strike (mark a spot: 12 missiles rain down, 18 each). X Flight Boost (sprint-fly at double speed; switches off when you stop sprint-flying; flight drains 2.5x while it runs) / Shift Meteor Dive (dive down: 15 + 1.5 per block fallen, up to 80). Z Solar Beam (30, x1.5 in daylight under open sky) / Shift Solar Flare (22 + fire + blind all round). V Gravity Tether (lift and hold a target 4 s, bosses 1.5 s) / Shift Singularity (a gravity grenade drags enemies within 7 blocks into its core, then implodes for 22). C Zero-G Field (6 s: enemies float helplessly); hold Shift+C folds it into its thruster pack. Reactor (v0.16.7): 1600 energy, +2.5/s, flight 2/s (4/s sprinting, 10/s with the Flight Boost). Packed: carry the Thruster Pack with no suit on and double-tap jump for a slow pack flight (no sprint, no fall damage) that uses 1 of the packed suit's charge a second.
projecthero.guide.iron_man.mark_4.body: The polished-gold deep-sea suit with a glass dome: water breathing, fast swimming, clear sight underwater and everything it does hits 1.5x harder in water -- on foot on land it is heavy and slow (Slowness I), but it flies like the Mk III (double-tap Space; 2 energy a second, 4 sprinting) on water-jet thrusters. Integrity 1600, absorbs 40%, reactor 1200 (2 a second). Moves:
projecthero.guide.iron_man.mark_v.body: Matte black and silent (no footsteps, no vibrations): mobs lose track of you, but the armour is paper thin. It flies like the Mk III (2 energy a second, 4 sprinting) on near-silent jets of air, and Shift+X Active Camo turns you and the suit invisible. Integrity 500, absorbs 15%, reactor 1000 (2.5 a second). Moves:
projecthero.guide.iron_man.combat.body: Any repulsor hit Staggers its target for 3 s (the Mk I's punch and flamethrower do it too): it slows, crackles with sparks, and your next punch on it deals bonus damage. Punch then repulsor within 1.5 s for extra knockback. As integrity falls the suit shows it: sparks below 60%, scorched cracked plating, smoke and a flickering glow below 35%, and a cracked visor on your HUD.

Unsuited with the Stark Glasses on, open the Call Armour picker and press PILOT on a full suit. It deploys as a drone and your view jumps into it: WASD flies, Jump / Sneak go up and down, Sprint boosts, click or R fires its repulsor. Your real body stays behind and can be hurt. The link ends if you press C, take damage or go past 96 m; the drone then flies back and docks in your inventory.

The Mk VI deploys from its briefcase. Gather all four pieces, then right-click one to pack them.
Iron Man armour only goes on with C, a suit call, the Briefcase or the Stark Gantry, and only comes off with C, the Stark Gantry or a send-home (it drops like any armour when you die). Every suit is at least diamond-grade, bulletproof against guns and gives 70% knockback resistance (the Hulkbuster 100%). There is no suit energy: integrity is the resource. While the suit has integrity it absorbs its share of every hit (20% Mk I ... 60% Hulkbuster) out of its integrity, 1:1; at 0 it is disabled -- no flight, no abilities, heavy Slowness, a dark visor -- until repaired. From the Mk III up the mob highlight switches on by itself with the helmet. A full suit gives Haste I in the Mk I, Mk II and Mk III, Haste II from the Mk IV Hydro up. An open faceplate snaps shut the moment you take off, use an ability or get hit.
projecthero.guide.green_lantern.dome_mod: Sneak + Z throws up a glowing hard-light dome around you: a green globe with a lattice of light that grows out over a second and a half, pushes out anyone who isn't in your squad, and flickers when it is close to breaking.
projecthero.guide.green_lantern.suits.bo: Press Sneak + N to open the suit screen and pick the suit your ring forms: the Default suit, the Corps Uniform, John Stewart or Classic Hal Jordan. Each card shows you wearing it. Your own face shows through every suit; the Corps Uniform and Classic Hal Jordan add a green domino mask, and John Stewart leaves your hands bare. The choice is saved. Pick one while suited and the ring re-forms the suit in the new style at once, at no charge. The Remove Ring button at the bottom of the screen (click it twice) takes the Power Ring off: the power leaves you and the ring goes back into your inventory, ready to be put on again or handed to someone else. Above it, the Body Glow and Flight Trail switches turn off the green glow around you in Ring Flight and the trail behind you when sprint flying (other players see your choice too).
Stormbreaker is already in your hands.

projecthero.guide.thor.stormbreaker.reca: Calling (v0.15.1): the first worthy player to carry a Stormbreaker binds it, one each -- a second axe stays unbound for another Thor, and one bound to someone else never changes hands by being picked up. R then calls Mjolnir and Stormbreaker interchangeably: if one is already with you (anywhere in your inventory or hands), R calls the other; if neither is, it calls whichever is closer -- one in another dimension counts as farthest but still comes if it is the only one; if both are with you, nothing moves. A called weapon flies home from anywhere -- the ground, a chest, another player, an unloaded chunk or another dimension -- never as a second copy, and takes your main hand, putting the other weapon back in your pack.
projecthero.guide.thor.stormbreaker.drop: On the ground (v0.15.3): like Mjolnir, a dropped Stormbreaker -- Q, dragged out of your inventory, lost when you die, or left behind by a throw with nobody to return to -- lies in the world as the axe itself. It never despawns or burns (in lava it floats up to the surface), only the worthy can lift it, by right-clicking it -- anyone else just hears it clang -- and R still calls it home from where it lies.

projecthero.guide.iron_man.glasses.body: Craft the Stark Glasses (two gold ingots over red stained glass pane, Basic Circuit, red stained glass pane), press Shift + N to open the Stark Gear screen and put them in the Eyes slot -- or just right-click them. They stay on under a suit. Wearing them you get automatic night vision, you can call your Mk IX Inferno and Hulkbuster I (the Sneak + C picker, the double-tap quick call, /ironman suit, Remote Pilot) -- the Hulkbuster drops in from orbit -- and Protocol Phoenix is armed. The Mk VIII Space armour is called with the Colantotte Bracelets, and the Mk VI Suitcase travels in its Briefcase.
projecthero.guide.iron_man.bracelets.bod: Store a Mk VIII Space armour on a Suit Platform and press the red Bracelets tab beside its menu to get the Colantotte Bracelets -- one pair, bound to you. Wear them in the Stark Gear slot instead of the glasses: they call ONLY the Mk VIII -- press C and its orbital pod is on its way (twice as fast as a normal call), lands beside you and fires the pieces onto you one by one. The call is free (suits have no energy) but uses the bracelets up. A Mk VIII you carry in your pack still wraps on in about 4 seconds with them on.
projecthero.guide.iron_man.phoenix.body: If you would die while not in a full suit, Protocol Phoenix stops the death, holds you still and calls in your best Mk VIII Space, Mk IX Inferno or Hulkbuster I (from your pack or a Suit Platform, even far away). Once it is on you are back on 5 hearts and the suit loses 10% integrity. It only works with your Stark Glasses on, needs that suit at 10%+ integrity, and recharges for 20 minutes.
